title: Chained onward control: a round-1 Pending spec candidate reading a yn71 %out2 rail keeps its stale mask -> _hl-over-rail silent miscompile
description:
CRITICAL verify-clean silent miscompile, reachable from clang -O1 (NOT hand-crafted). INTRODUCED BY yn71 (pre-yn71 the chained region blanket-declined via declineReClassifiedControl; yn71 lowers it and exposes this hole). ORTHOGONAL to 9paa (confirmed by git-stash A/B: identical on the pre-9paa plugin).

REPRO (2-file, clang -O1): caller: q=cq_theta; int y=5; if(q>5) y=ext_f(7); int w=6; if(y>50) w=ext_f(7); z=gg(w,q); m1=measure(z); m2=measure(y); return m1+m2;  lib: int ext_f(int a){return a+100;} int gg(int a,int b){return a*b;}. The second measure(y) keeps region-1's merge live so clang -O1 materializes BOTH rails.

MECHANISM: region1 (if q>5) is a 6.5 classical-call arm -> %out (round-1 rail, in the frozen reseed set). region2 (if y>50, cond reads %out) is CLASSICAL-conditioned at round-1 detect -> skipped -> survives round-1 flatten; the 2nd propagation taints its cond so yn71 detectAndLowerOnwardControl lowers it -> %out4 (a genuine quantum rail, two cqrt_copy_i32_controlled under flag icmp(%out,50)). gg(w=%out4, q) is a ROUND-1 Pending candidate (reads q, mask 0b10). At reseed-computation time (BEFORE the yn71 fixpoint) w=region2-merge-phi is untainted -> NOT in the frozen reseed set, so replanReseedSpecialization SKIPS gg (its ReadsReseed gate fails). After yn71 taints %out4, gg reads a quantum %out4 but its mask stays 0b10. declineTaintEscapes CARVES gg (shouldSpecialize=true, it is Pending) rather than declining. The step-262 driver clones stale-mask @__cq_q_gg_10 with body cq_template_mul_i32_hl(q_handle, %out4) -> reads %out4's i32 HANDLE-TAG as a classical literal. Trace: 'cq_template_mul_i32_hl(h0, 7) -> h11' computes q*7 (7 = handle-id of the %out4 rail h7) instead of the QQ multiply q*out4. opt exit 0, verify-clean, measure returns 0, WRONG UNITARY.

ROOT CAUSE: the round-2 reseed set is FROZEN before detectAndLowerOnwardControl (yn71) runs, so a yn71-produced rail %out4 is not in it; replanReseedSpecialization (0vvq) only re-plans Pending candidates reading the frozen reseed set, so a Pending candidate whose arg becomes tainted via a yn71 rail keeps its stale mask. yn71's clearance assumed 'spec-off-a-round-2-rail declines cleanly via kMsgUnknownCallee' but that only holds for a NEW candidate (not in Pending); a ROUND-1 Pending candidate is CARVED, not declined.

FIX DIRECTIONS (owner to choose): (a) MINIMAL SAFE DECLINE — after the yn71 fixpoint, recompute taintArgMask for every plan6.Pending candidate against FINAL taint; if it grew, the frozen mask is stale -> loud-decline (over-declining is safe, Prime Directive). (b) PROPER RE-PLAN — re-run replanReseedSpecialization (+9paa redetect) against final taint with an expanded reseed set that includes the yn71-produced UntaintedMergeRails (a combined spec/control fixpoint), re-widening gg 0b10->0b11 to bare-QQ, declining only a newly-tainted non-i32 arg. Needs its own PRD + red-green fixtures + Rule-13 clearance (core lowering change).

Discovered by the 9paa Rule-13 adversarial workflow (dedup-pending-diagnosed dimension), independently reproduced + escalated to clang -O1 by the verifier + by me (git-stash A/B attribution).
close_reason: FIXED + Rule-13 cleared. Reordered repropagateControlMerges so the reseed set is computed AFTER detectAndLowerOnwardControl (yn71), so a round-1 Pending spec candidate reading a yn71 %out2 rail is re-widened to bare-QQ instead of cloned with a stale _hl-over-rail mask. 3 fixtures + 1 e2e; the combined 9paa+afmv Rule-13 (8 dims, 0 defects) cleared it.

title: lowerShadowMemory SIGSEGV (use-after-free) on straight-line self-referential tainted-index store/load alloca sequence
description: Found by the lf8s Rule-13 adversarial review (2026-07-17, skeptic-confirmed): a STRAIGHT-LINE (no loop) sequence 'store i32 %acc, gep(%arr, %acc); %v = load gep(%arr, %q)' over an alloca [4 x i32] with tainted %acc/%q crashes cq-lowering with SIGSEGV (exit 139) — opt -passes=verify reports 'Call parameter type does not match function signature' and with -disable-verify the crash is a use-after-free in Module::print/TypeFinder. PRE-EXISTING: reachable on hand-written straight-line input (repro shadowstraight.ll in the lf8s review artifacts, session 7d583c33 tmp) — NOT introduced by the Lever-B unroll pre-pass; the pre-pass's U2b fence now keeps the rolled form away from it (lowering_unroll_leave_shadow_store_loop.ll pins the loud L3 decline). Suspect: lowerShadowMemory's handling of a store whose VALUE operand also feeds the INDEX of the same access web (self-referential), erasing an instruction still referenced. Crash-on-valid-input = must fix or loud-decline (Prime Directive).
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: sorenwilkening
comments.text: FIXED at f6d85b9. Root cause: BOTH QRAM emitters (processShadowAlloca + lowerQramReads) resolved the access index from a classify-time-captured Value* (A.RawIndex/R.RawIndex); an earlier access's RAUW (load -> new cqrt_qram_load) rewrote the live IR but not the capture, so the new call referenced the original load, which the deferred erase deleted -> dangling operand -> verifier UAF SIGSEGV. The 7z9k.3 Inc-3 fix covered only the store VALUE operand; this was its INDEX twin, biting exactly when the gep index is the load result DIRECTLY (a widening sext/zext in between stays live and gets RAUW-fixed, which is why the suite never caught it). Fix: re-read the index fresh from the LIVE gep's trailing operand at emit time (matchAddressGep proves RawIndex IS that operand, so fresh == captured modulo RAUW). Classification untouched -> accept surface identical. The nested QROM twin tbl2[tbl1[q]] crashed identically and is fixed+pinned too. Rule-13: 22-agent board (stale-operand-completeness Fable-xhigh w/ 11 probes incl. cross-alloca both orders, cross-emitter both directions, guarded-store, cast webs; quantum-semantics Fable-xhigh with per-basis-state LIFO trace of the idx==val aliased store; over-accept probes; fixture Rule-12; blast-radius) + skeptic refutation: 0 miscompiles/crashes/over-declines. Fixtures: lowering_qram_selfref_store_index.ll (repro web + distinct idx/val pin + LIFO reversal CHECKs), lowering_qram_read_nested_index.ll. Board residuals (no action needed, recorded): dead capture fields Accepted.RawIndex/ShadowAccess.{RawIndex,StoreVal} are optional future cleanup; stale Tainted/BirthOrder keys after erase filed separately.

title: In-place reversible arithmetic strategy — loop-rail self-update (add/xor immediate)
description:
Prerequisite for y05j.2 (owner decision 2026-06-26, after Bennett.jl source verification). The MISSING arithmetic-strategy axis: PARITY_MAP records CQ has "zero gate-strategy axis" while Bennett auto-dispatches in-place vs out-of-place adders. CQ lowers EVERY value op OUT-OF-PLACE (`cq_template_<op>_<W>_hl(q,c) -> FRESH handle`, verified e2e `add_i32_hl(h0,1)->h1`), so a loop-carried value rail self-update (`q = q ^ c` / `q += c`) threads a FRESH handle through the header phi each iteration = the X1 cross-iteration dirty rail (799w.3), which CANNOT be rolled-reverse-played (the per-iteration handles have no individual SSA identity, so emitInverseChain can't address iteration-k's rail to emit its _unc; the only alternatives leak+dephase or need an O(K) handle array = give up dynamic-K). This blocks y05j.2's whole-loop reverse-play (PRD-7.4 §2.2/§2.3).

ROOT CAUSE / FIX (Bennett-verified): Bennett's default Cuccaro adder is IN-PLACE — `(a,b,0)->(a,a+b,0)`, b OVERWRITTEN with the sum, a preserved, self-cleaning ancilla (src/adder.jl:21,49-60: "b is overwritten and holds the result; the original b value is gone"). It dispatches in-place when the result overwrites a DYING operand, out-of-place (lower_add!, fresh result) when a live operand must survive. The in-place strategy makes the loop rail ONE handle -> an "in-place-gated persistent rail" that satisfies the owner SOUND-ROLLED INVARIANT ([[owner-dynamic-circuits-in-model]]: only in-place-gated rz/ry/x/cnot persistent state may cross the backedge) -> the rolled DYNAMIC-K reverse-play becomes realizable.

SCOPE (owner 2026-06-26: loop-rail self-update ONLY — minimal blast radius, NO straight-line golden churn): recognize a loop-carried tainted rail whose latch-incoming is `q_next = q OP c` where (a) q is the header rail phi, (b) the OTHER operand is CLASSICAL (untainted), (c) OP in {xor, add, sub} is an in-place bijection given c, (d) old q is dead except through the rail (Case-A-style closure: only consumers are this op / the rail phi / measure / escape). Lower it IN-PLACE: emit a void one-handle in-place op instead of the out-of-place template, RAUW q_next -> q_handle, collapse the rail phi (Case-A style). The body then runs rolled in place — a VALUE accumulator, the twin of the 7.3 phase accumulator (slice_loop_phase_accum). Straight-line `y = x + 1` stays OUT-OF-PLACE (unchanged); a live-operand / non-classical-operand / non-bijection-op shape DECLINES (Prime Directive).

ABI (via tools/opcode_table.yaml, Rule 15 — minimal): in-place void one-handle add/xor immediate, e.g. `cqrt_add_<W>_inplace(h, imm)` / `cqrt_xor_<W>_inplace(h, imm)`. NO _unc/_inv twins needed: EmitInverse inverts xor by RE-EMISSION (self-inverse, like cqrt_x) and add by NEGATING the immediate (like the rotation-negate `cqrt_ry(h,-theta)` case) — two new EmitInverse branches mirroring existing patterns. Handles always i32 (Rule 15).

DELIVERS: rolled in-place value-accumulator loops = the X1 self-update subcase of 799w.3 via the in-place route, SUPERSEDING static-K unroll for this subcase (the two-quantum `acc = acc + q` Cuccaro case — in-place adder over a live quantum operand — stays a follow-on). y05j.2's break capture (R/idx copy-not-move + index gate) + whole-loop reverse-play then builds on the in-place rail (the reverse-play is realizable ONLY when rail+R+idx are all fixed in-place handles).

DONE CRITERIA: a classically-bounded value-accumulator loop `for(i<n) q = q ^ c; return cq_measure(q)` (and the `+= c` add form) lowers ROLLED, byte-identical to manual unroll (the slice_loop_phase_accum twin e2e golden); positive lit fixture + >=1 e2e golden; decline fixtures (live-operand keeps-source / non-classical-operand / non-bijection op) each mirror-exact (Rule 12). RULE-13: the in-place lowering + the EmitInverse add-negate/xor-reemit branches are core-spine changes — independent adversarial review before commit (a wrong inverse immediate or a mis-scoped in-place dispatch over a live operand is a verify-clean silent miscompile).

Emit, for a recognized single value-arm break loop: (1) mint O(1) carried rails R=cqrt_alloc_<W>(0) + first-break index idx=cqrt_alloc_iN(0) (idx==0 = not-yet-fired); (2) in-body, after brk computed: fire=brk AND (idx==0) (cqrt_toffoli); COPY-NOT-MOVE rail->R via cqrt_copy_<W>_controlled(fire,rail,R) (rail left INTACT); idx<-i+1 under fire; UNCOMPUTE scratch IN-ITERATION (fire via idx==i+1, idx==0 eq-flag, brk via cond(rail)) so the body is a clean per-iter unitary on (rail,R,idx); (3) exit consolidation cqrt_copy_<W>_controlled(idx==0,rail,R); (4) out=cqrt_copy_<W>(R), RAUW exit phi->out; (5) WHOLE-LOOP REVERSE-PLAY: backward-counted companion loop, body=emitInverseChain of the forward body, n times -> R/idx/rail->|0>; cqrt_free R,idx. NEW machinery = whole-loop reverse-play (3rd uncompute schedule beyond 7.3 Case A/B). NO new ABI. Carried ancilla O(1); dynamic-K. Risks (PRD §6): reverse-play wrong count; scratch O(K) if not in-iteration-uncomputed; non-idempotent first-fire; phase copied out; exit-phi dangling; LoopInfo perturbed by companion loop. e2e golden slice_loop_break.c (trace: forward body xn, capture, copy-out, reverse body xn, balanced frees). MUST clear independent adversarial Rule-13 review before commit (green suite insufficient). bd memories: 7.4-break-design-crux, 7.4-break-capture-resource.
acceptance_criteria: single value-arm break lowers rolled with index-gated copy-not-move capture + whole-loop reverse-play; O(1) carried ancilla; per-iter scratch |0> at backedge; R/idx/rail end |0>; out disentangled; zero measurements; e2e golden byte-clean; Rule-13 cleared.
close_reason: Emission done + the re-review miscompiles fixed/merged (rwou, PR #1). Properly Rule-13 cleared now; only the non-bug coverage follow-up x1t1 remains, tracked separately.

title: BUG (silent miscompile): local alloca QRAM array leaks stores when a loaded value is returned/measured -> dephasing
description: CORE LOWERING correctness defect found during Bennett-parity work (context: docs/design/bennett-parity/PARITY_MAP.md), GROUND-TRUTHED by running the pass. SCENARIO: a non-main function allocates a LOCAL array (alloca [N x iW]), does tainted-index store(s), loads v=a[j], and RETURNS or MEASURES v while the array POINTER does NOT escape. CURRENT WRONG BEHAVIOR: opt exits 0 and the whole array DAG is left allocated - stores NOT reversed (no cqrt_qram_store_W_unc), load not uncomputed, nothing freed. The returned v stays ENTANGLED with the leaked local scratch array; for the superposed-cell case (the whole point of the tainted-store Shadow path) tracing out the dead array DEPHASES v: a verify-clean silent miscompile under downstream interference (Grover/QPE). ROOT CAUSE: the reverse-vs-leak decision is keyed on the LOADED VALUE escape, not the ARRAY HANDLE ownership. (1) isInPlaceGateOn (ChainWalk.cpp) recognizes cqrt_qram_store_ but NOT cqrt_qram_load_, so the array handle is never a terminal and the load result becomes the data terminal. (2) DagTraversal.cpp:175 sets D.Escaped=true on a ReturnInst user of the load result. (3) Uncomputation.cpp:262 bails the ENTIRE DAG when D.Escaped, so the dead local stores leak too. This OVERTURNS recorded design decision 6 in the 7-5-qram-design-decisions memory, which conflated a returned VALUE HANDLE (caller owns its reversal) with a LOCAL SCRATCH ARRAY (caller cannot reach it, so cannot own it). FIX (decouple array-store-reversal from loaded-value-escape): for a local non-escaping-pointer alloca array, stores are dead scratch and MUST reverse regardless of whether a loaded value is observed. Mechanism = method-B copy-out (Rule 7 / Rule 14, reuse cqrt_copy_W + the value-arm reverse-play / whole-DAG LIFO spine): insert cqrt_copy_W of the load result into the escaping return rail, which makes the load+store DAG dead so it reverses wholesale (load_unc then store_unc LIFO, then cqrt_free); the copy output is the clean escaped return, disentangled from the now-zeroed array. GATES: CORE change to the escape/uncompute spine (Uncomputation/DagTraversal/ChainWalk) - Rule-13 territory; needs INDEPENDENT adversarial clearance, a green suite does NOT clear it. RED-GREEN: the exact shape (return a value loaded from a local tainted-index alloca array in a non-main fn) is currently UNTESTED; existing fixtures (lowering_qram_store_alloca_i32.ll etc.) ASSERT the leak via CHECK-NOT cqrt_qram_store_i32_unc with a MEASURE form - those flip to assert reversal. PRESERVE: a genuine array-POINTER escape (pointer returned/stored out) still leaks unchanged; const-global QROM (nothing to uncompute) unchanged - the fix is ONLY for local-scratch arrays. INTERIM DECLINE: skipped per owner 2026-06-24 since the uncompute fix lands directly. FALLBACK: if this fix stalls across sessions, add a loud decline for this shape as a safety valve rather than leave the silent miscompile live.
acceptance_criteria: Local non-escaping alloca array with a returned/measured loaded value: stores reverse (cqrt_qram_store_W_unc) in LIFO, the load is copied-out (cqrt_copy_W) + uncomputed, the array is freed, and the returned value is the disentangled copy; opt -verify clean + golden e2e trace diff clean. Genuine array-pointer escape still leaks (unchanged); const-global QROM unchanged. Mirrored red-green lit fixtures (previously leak-asserting fixtures flipped + a new return-form fixture). Rule-13 INDEPENDENT adversarial clearance of the escape/uncompute-spine edit.
close_reason: FIXED + Rule-13 CLEARED (commit 3abdaa0). Method-B copy-out for a load result directly escaping a non-main fn via ret/cq_measure: ChainWalk::isCopyOutSink makes cqrt_copy a source-preserving sink so the LOCAL array's load+store chain uncomputes via the existing dead-array reversal; array handle left clean |0>. 3 lit fixtures (2 measure-form flipped + return-form) + a non-main e2e slice (slice_qram_local_uncompute) that LINKS+RUNS the reversal; all 477 lit + 42 ctest green. Independent adversarial review refuted all 9 attack vectors + the shared-benign-set cross-check (value-arm/switch-value/Bennett-wrap unaffected). QRAM design-decision 4/6 corrected in memory 7-5-qram-design-decisions. Inc-1 scope = DIRECT sole-user ret/measure; the indirect arith-then-return / fan-out residual is follow-up test_C_libtooling-l6xk.

title: PRD-7.2 persisting-ret boundary: disposition matrix + explicit accept predicate
description:
# PRD-7.2 persisting-`ret` boundary: disposition matrix + explicit accept predicate

Adversarial review (2026-06-22, 15+ `clang -O1` probes + 3 code audits, fork
workflow) of PRD-7.2 "controlled function-return" surfaced an **accept/decline
boundary ambiguity** around returns that persist in a conditional arm. PRD edits
landed in `docs/prd/phase-07-expressiveness/PRD-7.2.md` (§2.3 correction note,
§2.6 deferral, §2.10 disposition matrix, new §2.11 accept/park predicate, §5/§6
reconciliation). This issue tracks the findings so the implementation honors them.

## Empirical ground truth (confirmed, not assumed)
`clang -O1` reconverges **every mergeable value early-return** to a single exit
(`select` or one merge-φ): verified across if-returns, switch-returns (all 5
variants — constants, computed values, printf, fall-through/`break`, opaque-call
arms — collapsed to ONE `ret`), nested-if, struct/sret, and non-sinkable
side-effect arms. The SCOPING-§4 "multiple `ret` / per-site return register" shape
**did not appear once** for mergeable values. A `ret` persists in an arm ONLY for a
genuine non-reconvergence reason — never a value-mux the pass must merge itself.

## Genuine persisting-`ret` survivors (the only ones that reach the pass)
- noreturn sink (`abort`/`exit`/`__assert_fail`/`llvm.trap`/`noreturn`) + `unreachable`, value sibling
- `musttail` return (ret glued to tail call by language rule) — TWO persisting value rets
- non-`abort` divergence (pure `for(;;)`) + value sibling
- phase-class value (`cq_phi`) returned beside an abort arm
- non-i32 / sret value (declined upstream by `declineTaintEscapes`)

## Findings (severity)
1. **[MAJOR] No stated accept predicate / no `PostDominatorTree`.** §6 Risk-2's
   mitigation "reconvergence proven by SSA/post-dominator identity" had no
   implementing analysis. Fixed: §2.11 A pins a purely-structural predicate
   (every arm ends in an unconditional `br` to a `soleMergePhi` merge; a
   `ret`/`unreachable` arm fails `uncondSucc` → cannot match accept).
2. **[MAJOR] `abort`+value matched TWO dispositions** — §2.8 park (accept) AND
   §2.10-disp-2 (decline). Resolved: §2.11 B discriminator — the noreturn-sink arm
   has no value and ends in `unreachable`, so there is nothing to merge → it is a
   **park** (accept), and the sibling `ret` is the ordinary uncontrolled return.
3. **[MAJOR] `musttail` partition missing.** The SAME source `if(f) return foo1();
   return foo2();` is a deliverable-1 **accept** when plain (clang merges) but
   produces TWO persisting value rets when `musttail` (decline-class). PRD never
   distinguished. Fixed: §2.10 row + §2.11 C-i (decline; reopenable tooling
   boundary — 7.2 does NOT synthesize the merge; a CFG-rewrite prepass would
   violate "detect before mutate").
4. **[MAJOR] §2.3 "exp2 gap" headline example is already handled.** `if(q>5)
   return q+1; return 3*q+7;` folds to `select` at -O1 and the existing 4.4
   `SelectMergeEmit` accepts it today (`opt` exit 0). The genuinely-new br-diamond
   surface is narrow + optimizer-cost-fragile. Fixed: §2.3 correction note;
   deliverable-1 fixtures must use a shape VERIFIED to survive as a br-diamond.
5. **[MINOR] Infinite-loop arm uncovered.** `if(q>5) return v; for(;;){}` produces
   the same "ret persists, no merge" CFG as abort but is NOT a recognized noreturn
   sink, NOT a value mux, NOT a bounded loop — fell into no bucket. Fixed: §2.10
   row → defer 7.3/7.4 (`"loop under quantum control"`).
6. **[MINOR/HAZARD] Phase value beside abort.** `p=cq_phi(q); if(q>5) return p;
   abort();` — whether the §2.8 cswap-park preserves the relative phase on the
   surviving `ret` is unproven. Fixed: §2.6 deferral + §2.11 C-iii — conservative
   loud decline (over-decline safe), resolve under Rule-13; do NOT silently route
   onto the in-place phase-escape path.
7. **[MINOR] Diagnostic precision.** A measurement-under-control early-return arm
   currently declines with the wrong message ("arm rewrites a condition operand")
   instead of a measurement-under-control message — §2.10 disp-4 requires a
   distinct source-located message + mirror-exact fixture.

## Confirmations (no change needed)
- `flattenRegion` is terminator-agnostic — a `ret`-terminated merge is already
  shipped green (`control_swap_ifelse_escape.ll` merge ends in `ret i32 %qm`). The
  PRD's "reuse-as-is" treatment of merge-ends-in-ret is CORRECT, NOT a new path.
- No mis-accept found in any of the 15+ probes; every persisting-ret shape declines
  loudly today (the safe pre-7.2 state).

## Implementation must-haves (Rule 12/13)
- Implement §2.11 A/B/C as the structural classifier; one mirror-exact negative
  fixture per §2.10 decline row (musttail value exit, infinite-loop arm,
  phase-beside-abort, measurement-under-control, §3c clobber).
- Deliverable-1 positive fixtures: a br-diamond VERIFIED to survive `-O1` (not
  fold-to-select, not taint-escape) for the data-mux path.
- Rule-13 clearance must confirm the (B) park-vs-(C) value-exit discriminator and
  the (iii) phase-park deferral, not assume them.
close_reason: DISCHARGED by Phase 7.2 Inc 1-4 (epic 65wb, closed) + owner decision 65wb.5. Verified 2026-06-23 by empirical opt probes + 11 green disposition-matrix fixtures. Finding-by-finding: (1) MAJOR no accept predicate -> §2.11-A is recoverRegion's purely-structural shape test (ret/unreachable arm fails uncondSucc, cannot match an accept); positive control_swap_value_ifelse.ll/control_swap_ifelse_escape.ll. (2) MAJOR abort+value double-disposition -> Inc 3 classifyAbortPark runs FIRST (sink arm no-value/unreachable = park) + Inc 4 both-arms-value-ret rule => abort-lookalike never mislabeled 'non-reconverging value exit'; Rule-13 cleared. (3) MAJOR musttail partition -> Inc 4 'non-reconverging value exit' (control_swap_reject_nonreconverging_value_exit.ll); 7.2 does NOT synthesize the merge (reopenable). (4) MAJOR exp2 headline already handled -> owner 65wb.5 DECLINE, Inc 1 'non-routable value multiplexer' (control_swap_reject_branch_datamux_exp2.ll). (5) MINOR infinite-loop arm -> Inc 4 'loop' (control_swap_reject_loop_under_control.ll), defer 7.3/7.4. (6) MINOR/HAZARD phase-beside-abort -> Inc 3 classifyAbortPark phase-class decline + Inc 4 phase row 'phase-class value escaping' (control_swap_reject_abort_phase_sibling.ll + control_swap_reject_phase_value_escaping.ll); Rule-13 cleared; never silently routed to the in-place phase path. (7) MINOR measurement-under-control diagnostic precision -> SUPERSEDED by PRD §2.10-final (measurement folds to existing source-located messages, NOT a new distinct string -- a blanket rename would REGRESS the precise 'impure phase arm'/'condition measured before the control route'/§3c-clobber diagnostics). Every measurement-under-control shape declines LOUDLY+source-located (no miscompile); Inc 4 improved the early-return case (now 'non-reconverging value exit', was clobber); fixtures control_swap_reject_measure_in_arm.ll + control_swap_reject_cond_datause_measure_early.ll. Must-haves all met: §2.11 A/B/C classifier (recoverRegion+classifyAbortPark+offPatternDisposition/classifyArms); 1 mirror-exact fixture per §2.10 decline row (all green); deliverable-1 positive shared-base br-diamond (control_swap_value_ifelse.ll); Rule-13 clearance of the (B)-park-vs-(C)-value-exit discriminator + (iii) phase-park deferral. See bd memory 7-2-offpattern-decline-partition + 7-2-abort-park-cascade.

title: One-register merge-phi lift bypasses the stale-record guard: lift RAUWs the phi to its base AFTER declineStaleRecordOps ran — lifted-phi consumer over a re-Ry'd wire lowers silently
description: Found by the test_C_libtooling-6j1 Rule-13 adversarial panel (2026-06-11), independently reproduced end-to-end from plain C at -O1. PRE-EXISTING (lift test_C_libtooling-5j5 + guard ordering; the 6j1 closure neither caused nor could see it). Shape: classical-condition diamond 'if (c) q = cq_phi(q0, th); b = cq_theta(q0, t2); v = q + 3;' -> merge %p = phi i32 [%qd,%arm],[%q,%entry] (one-register: both incomings on %q's wire), then %q2 = cq_theta(%q,t2) (sibling Ry), then %v = add i32 %p, 3. CHAIN OF HOLES: (1) declineStaleRecordOps (runs at CQLoweringPass guard stage) seeds the wire walk at %p — a PHINode is not a cq_phi CALL, so the 6j1 backward closure is a no-op, and the forward user-edge walk from %p never reaches theta(%q) -> op accepted; (2) declineClassicalMuxes (later, post-control) LIFTS the one-register merge phi (liftOneRegisterMergePhi, TaintPropagation.cpp) and RAUWs %p -> %q; (3) nothing re-runs the stale guard after the lift — the lift's comment 'every later guard still adjudicates it' is FALSE for declineStaleRecordOps, which is an EARLIER guard. RESULT: exit 0, verify-clean, cq_template_add emitted immediately AFTER cqrt_ry(t2) on the same handle while %p's record is pre-t2 on BOTH phi paths — the stale-record miscompile through the lift gateway. Controls: the unroutable-phi variant declines loudly via the mux guard, the phi-less twin declines via the stale guard — ONLY the lift gateway is silent. FIX DIRECTIONS (panel): (a) extend the backward seed closure to cross PHINodes the lift would prove one-register (phi-as-pure-renaming is exactly what the lift itself proves), or (b) re-run declineStaleRecordOps (or a targeted re-check of lifted-phi consumers) after declineClassicalMuxes — mind opt-exits-at-first-DS_Error message-ownership for existing fixtures either way. Red-green: decline fixture for the lifted shape + positive twin (op before the sibling Ry accepts after lift). Core change — Rule 13 adversarial clearance required.

title: Stale-record guards blind to chained-theta SIBLING records: op over a cq_theta-result record misses a later sibling Ry on the parent wire (theta-hop closure gap, straight-line + condProvenance)
description: Found while implementing test_C_libtooling-6j1 (2026-06-11), reproduced on the post-6j1 tree; CONFIRMED + EXTENDED by the 6j1 Rule-13 adversarial panel (4 lenses, independent reproduction, incl. end-to-end from plain C at -O1). The cq_phi-only seed closure stops at the seed's RECORD BOUNDARY (first non-cq_phi ancestor); a chained theta is MID-WIRE, so a sibling Ry behind it is invisible to every stale guard. FOUR confirmed verify-clean over-accept surfaces, all sharing this one root cause: (S1) STRAIGHT-LINE, no alias: %q=theta(u0,t1); %q2=theta(%q,t2); %q3=theta(%q,t3); %d=add %q2,3 — exit 0, cq_template_add emitted AFTER cqrt_ry(t3) while %q2 names the post-t2/pre-t3 record (repro /tmp/theta_sibling_gap.ll). (S2) ALIAS-OVER-THETA: %qd2=cq_phi(%q2,1.0) consumed instead — the exact 6j1 family one theta hop up; closure from %qd2 stops AT %q2, sibling unreachable. (S3) REGION/ROUTED-BASE twin: control_swap_reject_value_stalebase_diamond.ll with the alias producer changed cq_phi->cq_theta (derived routed base = theta result %q2=cq_theta(%q,1.0), pre-branch sibling %q3=cq_theta(%q,0.25)) is ACCEPTED and emits a full method-B routed stream whose route-in cqrt_cswap fires after ry(0.25) — ArmClassify's routed-base guard seeds {%q2}, closure stops at the theta hop. (S4) CONDITION-SIDE mint: condProvenance stops AT a theta call without entering its tainted arg-0 (right for sources, blind for chained thetas) — condition reads %q2 with sibling %q3 before the branch: phase region accepted, flag minted from the post-t3 wire (cq_template_icmp_hl AFTER ry(t3)) = MINT_AT_COMPARE P2 family (wrong arm fires AND icmp_inv cannot strip; the one-hop versions are pinned PERMANENT declines, control_swap_reject_stalecond_*.ll). FIX SKETCH (refined by the panel): cross theta hops in the closure but EXEMPT ON-ANCESTRY gates from the user frontier — only OFF-ancestry siblings are stale evidence; the producer over-decline the 6j1 comments fear comes only from flagging ancestor thetas, not siblings. The panel hand-traced that this preserves both accept twins (lowering_stale_record_alias_producer.ll, lowering_stale_record_add_before_theta.ll). Position-aware mode keeps the provably-post-emission accept; position-free mode (condition + routed base) has no emission point, so the exempt set is gates at-or-before the record producer in the opaque-call order. ALTERNATIVE (cruder, always sound): loudly decline >1 in-place theta consumer per handle (theta fan-out). Where: WireWalk.cpp closure + condProvenance (ArmClassify.cpp). Red-green: decline fixtures per surface S1-S4 + positive twins (op before sibling Ry accepts; producing theta NEVER flagged; on-ancestry multi-theta chains keep lowering). Core-detection change — Rule 13 adversarial clearance required. The 6j1 code comments (WireWalk.{h,cpp}) explicitly reference this issue as the known-open boundary.
close_reason: Fixed 2026-06-11: WireWalk::findNonDiagonalWireGate crosses chained-cq_theta arg-0 hops backward (per-seed, on-ancestry-exempt), flagging off-ancestry sibling thetas. Closes S1-S4 at the one shared walker (condProvenance untouched). Rule-13 cleared (OLD-vs-NEW A/B proved purely-additive-in-declines; multi-seed/termination/S3-S4/§3c all sound). See bd memory stale-record-chained-theta-closure-6vk.

title: Stale-record guard misses sibling-diagonal-alias wires: straight-line tainted op over a cq_phi alias of a re-Ry'd handle lowers silently (WireWalk seeding gap)
description: Found by the WI-5 §8 adversarial review (2026-06-11), reproduced on the current tree. Shape (straight-line, NO control flow): %q=cq_theta(u0,t1); %qd=cq_phi(%q,1.0); %q2=cq_theta(%q,t2); %v=add %qd,3; measure(%v); measure(%q2). The pass ACCEPTS (exit 0) and emits cq_template_add_i32_hl(%h,3) AFTER cqrt_ry(%h,t2) — the template reads the POST-Ry wire while %qd names the PRE-Ry record: exactly the physics lowering_reject_stale_record_add.ll mandates as a loud decline ('operand predates a non-diagonal gate'). ROOT CAUSE: OpcodeLowering::declineStaleRecordOps seeds WireWalk::findNonDiagonalWireGate from the op's operands (%qd); the walk is FORWARD-only, and the chained theta consumes the SIBLING SSA name %q, so a walk seeded at %qd never reaches it. condProvenance has the same theta-stop blindness (by design for sources, wrong for CHAINED thetas with a tainted arg-0). FIX SKETCH: close every seed BACKWARD through diagonal cq_phi arg-0 hops to the wire origin before walking forward (the closure ArmClassify's diagonalAliasHit/WI-5 stale-base guard already walks) — either inside findNonDiagonalWireGate or at the declineStaleRecordOps seeding site; mind the position-aware mode's dominance proof (the closure must not flag the theta that PRODUCES a compared/consumed record — only gates AFTER the record; see the WI-5 analysis: seeding at the parent record wrongly includes the producing gate, so close through cq_phi hops ONLY, never through theta hops). The control-path twins (value diamond/if-else routed base) are ALREADY closed by the WI-5 routed-base guard in ArmClassify (control_swap_reject_value_stalebase_{diamond,ifelse}.ll); this issue is the remaining STRAIGHT-LINE surface (and any other declineStaleRecordOps consumer). Red-green: decline fixture mirroring lowering_reject_stale_record_add.ll through one rz-alias hop, plus a positive twin (theta BEFORE the record op accepts). Core-detection change — Rule 13 adversarial clearance required. Repro file preserved at /tmp/wi5_stale_straightline.ll (regenerate from this description if gone).
close_reason: Landed: WireWalk diagonal-alias seed closure (cq_phi-hops-only, record-boundary stop) + ArmClassify manual-closure removal + 7 fixtures (2 decline, 2 accept twins, 2 re-pointed WI-5, 1 inarm companion, 1 exclusive-arms pin). Adjacent pre-existing gaps filed: test_C_libtooling-6vk (theta-hop, 4 surfaces), test_C_libtooling-2qyz (merge-phi lift bypass). Memory: wirewalk-diagonal-alias-closure.

title: Uncompute: dead sibling chain emits adjoint+free BEFORE a later measure of the lineage's live handle (free-before-measure)
description: PRE-EXISTING (found+reproduced during the WI-4 §8 adversarial review, 2026-06-11; NOT introduced by the swap-route value path — reproduces straight-line with no control region). Shape: a DEAD tainted template result whose lineage walks back through a handle that is LATER measured. Repro: %q=cq_theta(...); %dead=add i32 %q,7; measure(%q) lowers to: alloc; ry; add_hl; add_hl_inv; cqrt_ry(-theta); cqrt_free(h_inv); cqrt_measure(h) — the whole-chain adjoint UNDOES the prep Ry and frees the register's wire BEFORE the user's measure reads it: a verify-clean silent miscompile (the measure sees |0>, not the prepared state) AND a Rule-5/6 violation (the free is a projective reset of a live register). Root cause: ChainWalk::forwardConsumerCount deliberately excludes measure sinks, so the measured upstream handle does not register as shared (HasFanOut stays false), and Uncomputation/FreePoint classify the dead terminal as Insert without checking whether any lineage handle has a measure/live reader positioned AFTER the candidate free point. Fix direction: a lineage handle with a measure user (or any reader) scheduled after the insert point must disqualify the chain (loud decline or skip) — the post-measure-gate discipline of Rule 6 applied to the whole recovered lineage. Probe preserved in the WI-4 review record; add a lit fixture lowering_uncompute_dead_sibling_premeasure.ll when fixing.
close_reason: Fixed 2026-06-11: recoverForwardChain scans non-terminal lineage handles for measure sinks; uncompute loud-declines (kMsgLineageMeasured) before emitting a free of a measured register. Rule-13 cleared (both lenses); keys only on cqrt_measure_ so control e2e goldens stay green. QQ-extension caveat in bd memory uncompute-lineage-measure-guard-3h8.

title: Pass-wide position-vs-SSA hazard: pure tainted producers lowered at their SCHEDULED position can read a stale pre-Ry record (verify-clean silent miscompile family)
description:
Family: a PURE tainted producer (add/sub/mul/casts/icmp) denotes, by SSA semantics, the value of its operands AT THE OPERANDS' DEFINITION — but the lowering emits its cq_template_* call at the instruction's SCHEDULED position in the block. Opaque cq_* calls keep their order; pure instructions do not (Rule 9). When a chained, tainted-operand cq_theta (an in-place, NON-diagonal Ry) sits between an operand's definition and the pure producer's position, the emitted template reads the post-Ry basis while the SSA value denotes the pre-Ry record: a verify-clean wrong unitary. Diagonal gates (cq_phi/Rz) between the two are harmless (basis-preserving) — non-diagonality is the load-bearing trigger (bd memory rz-diag-flag-strip-invariant).

Two confirmed-live probes (both accepted, exit 0, full lowering, 2026-06-10):

1. IN-GUARD instance (FIXED by test_C_libtooling-ee5 review round 2): derived branch condition
     %q  = cq_theta_si32(%u0, 0.5)
     %q2 = cq_theta_si32(%q, %t2)    ; chained Ry on the wire
     %d  = add i32 %q, 1             ; stale %q hidden behind the pure add
     %c  = icmp sgt i32 %d, 5
     br i1 %c, ...
   Emitted cq_template_add_i32_hl(%h, 1) AFTER cqrt_ry(%h, %t2). Closed by seeding ArmClassify's wireGainsNonDiagonalGate from the condition's full tainted provenance (condProvenance) instead of the compare's direct operands; fixture control_swap_reject_stalecond_derived_cond.ll. THIS GUARD COVERS ONLY CONDITIONS OF DETECTED CONTROL REGIONS.

2. STRAIGHT-LINE instance (OPEN — this issue; no branch, outside ArmClassify's reach entirely; OpcodeLowering/TaintPropagation domain):
     q = cq_theta(u0, g); q2 = cq_theta(q, t2); d = q + 1; measure(d);
   Silently accepted today: cq_template_add fires post-Ry while d = q+1 denotes the pre-Ry record. Same stale-record family, zero control flow involved, so no ArmClassify guard can ever see it.

Likely shape of a fix (to be designed, NOT prescribed here): before lowering any tainted pure op, walk each tainted operand's forward in-place-gate wire (the cq_phi-transparent / cq_theta-blocking walk now in ArmClassify::wireGainsNonDiagonalGate) and LOUDLY DECLINE if the wire gains a non-diagonal gate between the operand's defining call and the op's position — or equivalently, decline any tainted pure op whose operand has a tainted-operand cq_theta user (position-free, conservative, over-decline-safe). Note the source semantics for the straight-line shape IS well-defined (an entangling record at the operand's wire window — see MINT_AT_COMPARE.md §0/P6), so a future ACCEPT would need wire-window emission placement, not just a guard; decline-first per the Prime Directive.

Design-of-record / evidence: docs/design/rssa-swap-control/MINT_AT_COMPARE.md (esp. §4 "position is not provenance"); oracle docs/design/rssa-swap-control/investigation_mint_at_compare.py (P2 quantifies the family: stream fidelity cos^2(t2/2) with a clean flag). Origin: reviewer feedback on test_C_libtooling-ee5, round 2 (2026-06-10).
notes: FIXED (pending review). Design choice the issue left open: POSITION-AWARE guard, not position-free. Rationale: a pure op's cq_template_* is emitted AT THE OP'S OWN scheduled position and opaque calls keep their order through the backend — so the inspected point IS the emission point (unlike the MINT_AT_COMPARE §4 trap, where the mint emits at the BRANCH while the guard reasoned from the COMPARE's schedule). Order proof per tainted operand's wire theta T vs op I: DT.dominates(I,T) AND !isPotentiallyReachable(T,I) — the second conjunct closes loop-iteration-2 staleness (template re-executes post-Ry while its SSA value is loop-invariant). Implementation: shared walker hoisted to ir-pass/{include,src}/WireWalk.{h,cpp} (ArmClassify = position-free mode, no phi-crossing, behavior unchanged; new guard = position-aware mode, crosses PHINode/select value-routing); guard = OpcodeLowering::declineStaleRecordOps, pure analysis run FIRST in both pipeline entry points (pre-RAUW: post-RAUW the pre/post-Ry SSA values collapse onto one i32 handle and the distinction is unrecoverable); declined ops recorded in taint.StaleDeclined, skipped by lowerOps. Diagnostic: 'cq opcode lowering: operand predates a non-diagonal gate' (DiagnosticInfoUnsupported, DS_Error, !dbg). Fixtures: lowering_reject_stale_record_{add,crossblock,loop}.ll (decline) + lowering_stale_record_add_{before_theta,after_phi}.ll (accept boundary: pre-theta schedule emission-exact per P1 wire-window argument; diagonal Rz transparent). NOTE: opt exits at the FIRST DS_Error, so control_swap_reject_stalecond_derived_cond.ll (whose stale add the new guard now catches first) was re-pointed to the new message, and a new companion control_swap_reject_stalecond_derived_cond_preadd.ll (add scheduled pre-theta — new guard silent) keeps ArmClassify's ee5 provenance seeding pinned. ir-pass-lit 113/113 green, e2e 5/5 green. MINT_AT_COMPARE.md §4/§5 updated.

title: Tainted rotation ANGLE: straight-line hole remains (broken-module exit 134 / handle-tag read) — guard RotationLowering + audit CastLowering's erase-all-users invariant
description: Found by the test_C_libtooling-9hh §8 adversarial clearance (2026-06-10). A quantum-derived value in a rotation's arg-1 ANGLE slot (e.g. %ang = sitofp(%q) or %ang = call double @ext(i32 %q), both TAINTED since taint propagates to any user) has NO fixed unitary — yet outside control regions nothing declines it. Two failure modes, both loud-but-wrong: (a) sitofp family: CastLowering cross-type-RAUWs f64->i32 assuming every user is itself lowered+erased, but a cqrt_rz/cq_template call holding the angle is FINAL — the mistyped call survives, LLVM ERROR Broken module, opt exit 134 (probe: straight-line %qd = cq_phi(%q, sitofp(%q)) with NO control flow); (b) opaque-call family: %ang = call double @ext(i32 %q) survives well-typed; after RotationLowering's RAUW it reads the i32 RUNTIME HANDLE — verify-clean, links, runs, prints a plausible trace with a fixed angle = f(handle_tag): the silent-miscompile class, in straight-line code. The REGION-level guard landed with 9hh (ArmClassify::taintedAngleGate + control_swap_reject_tainted_angle{,_underived,_prebase}.ll); this issue is the straight-line root fix: decline loudly ('cq rotation lowering: unsupported ...' or a dedicated 'rotation angle' diagnostic) in RotationLowering::emitRz / lowerRotations when arg-1 is in Taint.Tainted, BEFORE any emission; mirror in cq_theta's angle. Also audit CastLowering's 'every user erased' invariant against emitter-minted final calls (the same violation family). Rule 12: ship with straight-line reject fixtures for both families.

title: Tainted gated switch with distinct per-case quantum handles silently miscompiles (merge-φ collapse drops edges)
description:
BUG (confirmed silent miscompile, clang -O1 reachable). A tainted-scrutinee GATED switch whose merge phi collects DISTINCT quantum handles per case (case0 -> qx, case1 -> qy, ...) is silently miscompiled: the result is collapsed to ONE handle and the other-case edges are dropped.

ROOT CAUSE. The merge-phi discriminator (ControlDetection.cpp:663-669) only checks that every incoming is TAINTED — never that they are the SAME base handle, despite the comment at 643-645 asserting "every incoming the same in-place handle". lowerGatedSwitch step-4 (ControlledLowering.cpp:348-358) then RAUWs the whole phi to the FIRST tainted incoming, silently dropping every other-handle edge. The gated path has NO value-mux (unlike the empty-arm/select-chain path's dissolveSelect).

REPRO (clang -O1, llvm@19 19.1.7, libCQPass.so @ b062f2d; /tmp/cqcheck/sw_distinct_q.c): switch on tainted s with case0 r=cq_phi(qx,.1), case1 r=cq_phi(qy,.2), default r=cq_phi(qx,.4); out=cq_phi(r,1.5). Per-arm gates are correct, but the merge phi RAUW-collapses to qx, so downstream cq_phi(r,1.5) -> cqrt_rz_i32(%h1/*qx*/,1.5) runs on qx unconditionally; qy abandoned. When s==1 the program operates on qx not qy. opt -verify CLEAN, exit 0, NO diagnostic.

EMPIRICAL FRAMING (2026-06-03). (1) Legitimate operation (coherent multiplexer over a quantum scrutinee), not malformed. (2) PURE selection of distinct handles already lowers correctly via the empty-arm mux (/tmp/cqcheck/pure_select.c). (3) Surface restriction can't help: clang -O1 gives IDENTICAL IR for switch / if-else-if / in-place-then-select (/tmp/cqcheck/{ifelse_distinct,inplace_then_select}.c). Trigger is the cross-handle MERGE.

RECOMMENDED FIX (re-scoped 2026-06-03 v2, user-chosen = LOWER CORRECTLY, Bennett MUX-EXCH / controlled-SWAP, FREE the sources).

NOTE — supersedes a v1 "XOR-copy + uncompute" plan, which is NOT physical here: copying a superposition (XOR or add) ENTANGLES the source with the result, and uncomputing the source's prep does NOT disentangle it (no-cloning). To MOVE the selected handle's state into the result AND free the source, the primitive is controlled-SWAP (Fredkin) = Bennett's MUX-EXCH "exchange" strategy (docs/bennett-jl-comparison.md lists MUX-EXCH distinct from copy for exactly this).

LOWERING (both-handle / all-tainted-handle merge):
  regOut = cqrt_alloc_<W>(0)
  for each DISTINCT base handle q (grouped by the arm(s) that select it):
      cqrt_cswap([OR of that arm's case eq-flags], regOut, q)   // controlled-SWAP: move q's state into regOut; q -> |0> in that branch
  RAUW merge phi -> regOut; route downstream uses to it.
Per-arm controlled GATES stay as today (applied before the move). MIXED/classical arms: a classical constant has no quantum source to free -> add/sub-seed (reuse dissolveSelect mux.1/WP4); the constant is trivially uncomputable.

NEW RUNTIME PRIMITIVE REQUIRED: cqrt_cswap (Fredkin / controlled-SWAP) + forward/controlled templates. This REVERSES the bd memory tainted-arm-select-mux-no-new-primitive ("no Fredkin needed") — that holds for the KEEP-SOURCES-LIVE select copy (mux.2), NOT for the FREE-THE-SOURCES move here.

HARDER SUB-PART (non-selected-source uncompute): controlled-SWAP frees only the SELECTED source per branch; NON-selected sources retain prepared state entangled with the scrutinee s (garbage that pollutes regOut's measurement). Fully cleaning them is the nontrivial Bennett/QROM-MUX-EXCH uncomputation (reverse each non-selected source's prep in its branch). Real design work — spike it.

SCOPE / STAGING. This has grown from "reuse dissolveSelect" to a FEATURE: (i) cqrt_cswap primitive (runtime + templates), (ii) MUX-EXCH gated lowering + detection routing, (iii) non-selected-source uncompute, plus (0) an IMMEDIATE interim DECLINE (require same-base-handle uniformity -> WP12 'switch under quantum control', over-decline-safe) to close the silent miscompile NOW while the feature is built (mirrors the mux-diag->mux precedent). Recommend splitting into sub-tasks (0)-(iii).

DETECTION. Discriminator at ControlDetection.cpp:663-669 routes a distinct-base-handle merge phi to the MUX-EXCH lowering (resolve each incoming via cq_phi->operand0 to its base; group by arm). UNIFORM-handle merges keep the cheap RAUW (no mux) — do not regress multihandle/shared/emptydefault.

RELATED. The free-vs-keep-live question also applies to the shipped select mux (mux.1/.2): they leave DEAD sources entangled (assumed live). If that is a concern, file a sibling. See docs/bennett-jl-comparison.md (MUX-EXCH/QROM) + bd memory tainted-arm-select-mux-no-new-primitive (now scoped).
acceptance_criteria: POSITIVE fixture lowering_control_switch_gated_distinct.ll (gated switch, distinct per-case quantum handles): asserts cqrt_cswap-based MUX-EXCH lowering — fresh cqrt_alloc_<W>(0) + per-arm controlled-SWAP moving each selected handle in (no dropped edge), selected source freed to |0>/disentangled, non-selected sources uncomputed, downstream uses the muxed register, opt -verify clean, result correct per scrutinee value. REGRESSION: uniform-handle gated fixtures (gated/_shared/_multihandle/_emptydefault) byte-identical (cheap RAUW, no mux). If staged, the interim decline asserts 'switch under quantum control' + CHECK-NOT cqrt_rz{{.*}}controlled. ir-pass-lit green.

description: Phase 4.3 audit re-sweep finding (pre-existing Phase-4-core silent miscompile + crash). clang canonicalizes if(u!=k)/if(!cond) to an inverted compare with SWAPPED branch targets, putting the single gate arm on the FALSE successor. Two bugs: (1) the control flag was the raw compare with gates fired on flag=1 — the NEGATION of the source condition (silent miscompile); (2) clang value-propagates the merge's straight-through edge to a known CONSTANT (e.g. if(u!=5) → entry edge = 5), so the gate φ RAUW'd to the constant instead of the handle → cq_measure(constant) crash. Fix: matchDiamond reports ArmIsFalse; substituteControlled fires the arm on ¬flag via the cqrt_x bracket when region.ArmNegated; dissolveBranchPhi RAUWs a gate φ to its TAINTED incoming (the handle), not the Pred edge. Compound/nested negated conditions were already correct (clang preserves the real icmp_ne predicate in the && form).

title: Fix opcode_table.yaml fcmp predicate set: one -> une (C != emits une)
description:
The fcmp predicate set in tools/opcode_table.yaml ships 'one' (ordered-not-equal) but Clang emits 'une' (unordered-not-equal) for C '!=' on floats at -O1 (no fast-math). Net effect: a tainted (float != float) lowers to cq_template_fcmp_une_<W>, which DOES NOT EXIST -> link failure; meanwhile the 8 generated _one_ symbols are dead (no -O1 C source emits them).

EVIDENCE (Apple clang 17, -O1 -emit-llvm):
  a == b -> fcmp oeq
  a != b -> fcmp une   <-- yaml has 'one', not 'une'
  a <  b -> fcmp olt
  a >= b -> fcmp oge
Runtime header today: grep -c _one_ = 8, grep -c _une_ = 0.

Accurate C float-comparison predicate set is {oeq, une, olt, ogt, ole, oge}. (ROADMAP's '14 predicates' is also wrong for the same reason — C emits exactly 6, one per operator.)

## Context
Surfaced during Phase 3 design dialogue (full opcode lowering). Predicate-flip canonicalization (Q4) maps une<->une, oeq<->oeq, olt<->ogt, ole<->oge for literal-on-left compares, so une must be present. Related to the Phase 3 opcode-lowering workstream and the eventual Phase 8 ABI freeze.
acceptance_criteria: predicates.fcmp in opcode_table.yaml yields 'une' so a tainted C float '!=' links; runtime/cq_templates.{h,c} regenerated via tools/gen_templates.py with the SHA preamble updated; a hand-written .ll (or e2e) fixture exercises a tainted float != float and FileChecks cq_template_fcmp_une_*. Decide as part of fix whether to also retain 'one' for future -ffast-math support or drop it (currently dead at -O1).
notes: Subsumed by Phase 3 WP1 (test_C_libtooling-cbn.2): the one->une fix is WP1's first deliverable. Close when WP1's yaml edit + regenerated header land. D2 resolved: drop 'one' now, re-add under fast-math later.

title: phase-2 WP3: RotationLowering module + delete MidHandleRebind + rewire
description:
The load-bearing change — after this the pass lowers the new surface end-to-end. Lands in the SAME commit as WP2 (PRD §6 commit 4).

NEW module ir-pass/src/RotationLowering.{cpp,h} — void lowerRotations(Module&, WidthDispatch&, TaintSet&):
- THETA (iterate taint.ThetaCalls in BB order; forward order matters for chains): classical operand -> alloc+ry, RAUW theta result to the i32 alloc handle, insert into Tainted, seed BirthOrder[h]=NextBirth++; tainted operand -> ry only, RAUW to the operand handle.
- PHI (iterate taint.PhiCalls, collected regardless of taint): tainted operand -> emit rz; classical -> no rz; RAUW to operand either way; erase.
- NEVER RAUW to the void ry/rz call. Diagnostics via DiagnosticInfoUnsupported (mirror MeasureLowering), leave call in place to surface at verifier.

INVARIANT (§1): cross-type RAUW (theta result -> i32 handle) is laundered by erasure — every tainted user is itself lowered to a handle-consuming call and erased before the verifier. Verify-clean on this assertions-OFF LLVM 19.1.7.

Removal + rewire (same commit):
- git rm MidHandleRebind.cpp/.h; CMakeLists drop it, add RotationLowering.cpp.
- OpcodeLowering: lowerOps(M,wd,taint) (drop RebindMap&); rebind.BirthOrder->taint.BirthOrder, rebind.NextBirth->taint.NextBirth; drop MidHandleRebind.h include. No logic/opcode-coverage change (add/fadd only).
- MeasureLowering: lowerMeasures(M,wd,taint); delete pattern (a) StructToHandle + pattern (b) insertvalue; keep pattern (c) (tainted i32 handle) + 'operand not recognized' diagnostic.
- TaintPropagation: resolveSources -> thetaFn/phiFn/measureFn; collectAndSeed pushes ThetaCalls (+seed worklist), PhiCalls (no seed), MeasureCalls.
- CQLoweringPass: include RotationLowering.h; early-out predicate includes PhiCalls (classical-only-phi must still run, else unresolved @cq_phi_* extern is a Stage-3 link error); order propagate -> lowerRotations -> lowerOps -> lowerMeasures -> dead-decl sweep; remove eraseDeadInits; runOnFunction shim filters all three lists.

Ref: IMPLEMENTATION.md §4 WP3, §1.
acceptance_criteria: Pass lowers the §2.1 slice end-to-end; -passes=verify clean on all fixtures; ir-pass-lit green (with WP4); grep cq_init|qint_mid_t|RebindMap empty (done-criteria 1-4,6).

title: cqc + e2e ctests: support Homebrew clang/opt names on macOS

title: ir-pass: link with -undefined dynamic_lookup on macOS
description: ir-pass/libCQPass builds as a MODULE library — out-of-tree pass plugin convention, opt/clang provide LLVM symbols at dlopen time. Linux's ld silently allows undefined symbols in .so modules, so the build succeeds. macOS's ld is strict: 'Undefined symbols for architecture x86_64: llvm::Value::replaceAllUsesWith, llvm::Instruction::eraseFromParent, etc.' Standard fix used by Polly, Enzyme, sanitizers: add '-Wl,-undefined,dynamic_lookup' as a link option, gated on APPLE in ir-pass/CMakeLists.txt. The IR pass doesn't actually depend on libLLVM at link time on either platform; macOS just needs the explicit allowance.

title: ir-pass: dispatch on Tainted set membership, not isa<ConstantInt>
description: Current step-5 dispatch in CQLoweringPass.cpp checks isa<ConstantInt>(B) to choose between cq_template_add_i32 and cq_template_add_i32_hl. This misses non-constant classical operands — e.g. function args, runtime-loaded values (scanf, globals) — which are also classical and should also dispatch to _hl. The taint set built in step 4 is the right predicate: if an operand is in Tainted it carries a quantum handle (symmetric); otherwise it is classical (use _hl, swap if needed so handle is lhs). Since taint sources are Alloc results and propagation only follows Instructions, a tainted add by construction has at least one tainted operand, so the 'both classical' branch is unreachable. Update step-5 dispatch + add a lit test exercising a non-constant classical operand (function arg).
close_reason: Closed

title: runtime+ir-pass: cq_template_add_i32_hl for handle+literal mixed-operand Q+C add
description: When the rhs of a tainted add is an LLVM ConstantInt (Q+C literal, or Q+C var folded by constprop), the runtime currently formats it as h%d, producing misleading traces like cq_template_add_i32(h0, h5) where h5 is the integer literal 5 (no such handle exists). Design (per soren 2026-05-24): add a dedicated runtime entry point cq_template_add_i32_hl(int32_t lhs_handle, int32_t rhs_literal) printing the rhs as a bare integer (no h prefix). IR pass dispatches: rhs isa ConstantInt -> _hl variant; rhs is a tainted SSA value -> existing symmetric cq_template_add_i32. Never promote classical->handle via cq_init_i32 (preserves future cq_alloc opt). Update PLAN.md §4.7.1/§6.3 to reflect the two-function design (kills the existing prose contradiction).

Output IR contains: cqrt_alloc_classical_i32 calls replacing @cq_init_i32; cqrt_template_add_i32 call replacing tainted add i32; cqrt_measure replacing @cq_measure. 5. title: 20xt.5 (e): residual tainted i32 select-chain in the (d)-flattened atan2l (fold-residue / SelectClassify)
description:
# 20xt.5 (e) — residual tainted i32 select-chain in the (d)-flattened atan2l

DISCOVERY (bd 20xt.5, blocker (d) landed): with (d) [PredMux tolerates
unreachable switch-defaults], atan2l's TOP-LEVEL now flattens COMPLETELY to
straight-line (@probe: 0 br/switch, @atanl hoisted as a direct call — VERIFIED
via CQ_DUMP_PRE_DETECT). The census note's blocker (e) is CONFIRMED REAL (not a
hand-edit artifact): the flattened @probe leaves a tainted i32 quadrant-index
select-chain that SelectClassify declines. CQ_CTRL_DBG pinpoints the offending
instruction:

    %45 = select i1 %44, i32 %16, i32 %15
  where %44 = and i1 %43, %27  and  %27 = and i1 false, %26   (constant-false!)
        %16 = or i32 0, %15                                    (identity: == %15)

ROOT CAUSE: `and i1 false, %x` and `or i32 0, %x` are FOLD RESIDUES minted by
cq-lowering itself (VERIFIED: 0 occurrences in the pre-cq-lowering inlined IR).
They come from cq-lowering's internal fp80-union promotion / foldConstantCones /
the PredMux flatten's plain `ConstantFolder` IRBuilder, and no InstCombine runs
after to clean them (PRD §6.1: no LLVM optimization between flatten and template
lowering). The residues make (i) `%44 = and %43, false = false` so `%45 =
select i1 false, ...` is a DEGENERATE select, and (ii) `SelectClassify::
collectCondTree(%44)` fails on the constant-`false` `and` leaf (not a compare) →
`diagnoseUnderControl(Sel, "control flow")`.

Since x=0.5L>0, the quadrant index m ∈ {0,1} = sign(y) — the whole i32
select-chain is a redundant re-derivation of a single bit; it would collapse
entirely under identity folding.

FIX CANDIDATES (each a core-lowering change → own Rule-13):
  (i)  Use `IRBuilder<InstSimplifyFolder>` (or manual identity folds) in the
       PredMux flatten's minting so `and false,X`→false, `or 0,X`→X, and the
       L1112 degenerate-select guard (currently SSA-identity-only) catches the
       semantically-equal arms. ELEGANT but broad (every minted node) — must
       preserve the no-NOT / and-or-over-compare-leaves predicate grammar.
  (ii) A targeted post-flatten identity-simplify sweep (extend
       foldConstantConesInFunction with `and false/true`, `or 0/-1`, `add/sub 0`,
       `xor 0`, degenerate `select c,a,a`, constant-condition select) — folds the
       residues while keeping the flatten's IRBuilder unchanged.
  (iii) Extend SelectClassify to accept the compound/degenerate condition — the
        LEAST attractive (it accepts a shape that should have folded away).

RULE-12: red-green — a lit fixture with a nested tainted region that flattens to
a degenerate `select i1 false` chain (positive: it lowers after the fold; the
current build DECLINES it, mirror char-for-char) + a probe that a genuinely
compound tainted condition still declines cleanly. Rule-13 per the flatten-core
change.

HONESTY: even with (e), atan2l STILL declines at (clone) — the inner-atanl
clone-control (9 internal branches + QROM reads under control). (e) advances
atan2l from (e) to (clone); it does NOT make atan2l compile. Census COMPILES
UNCHANGED.

comments.text:
RULE-11 RE-DERIVATION of coshl->expl @ -O1 (2026-07-17, branch 3c6m.14-control-l6). CORRECTS the model in my 07-17 06:26 comment: the residual is NOT "just the Shadow half re-run on the clone body". Three IR-confirmed facts (debug-dumped the module right after the promoteFp80Union fixpoint):

(1) promoteFp80Union ALREADY runs on @expl at module level. It iterates EVERY function, and vqlq's AdmitArgDerived admits expl's UNTAINTED fp80 Argument seed. It promotes 3 of expl's 9 unions (12 i80 bitcasts appear). So "the clone body is never seen because the arg is untainted" is NOT the mechanism — the hypothesis in the task/06:26-comment is wrong on this point.

(2) The OTHER 6 unions are shapes promoteFp80Union DELIBERATELY declines — two documented over-safe declines that survive as MEMORY (so scanBody then rejects the alloca as "unsupported instruction"):
   - SIGN-EXTRACT reads (GET_LDBL80): offset-8 expsign word read via `shl i64 w,48; ashr exact i64 _,48; trunc nsw to i32`. The §4.1 PaddingWalk over-safely declines any `exact` shift on a padding-diverged operand (documented "over-safe by choice").
   - INTEGER-SEEDED SET_LDBL packs (floorl reconstruct): NO `store x86_fp80` seed; instead `load i64 @off8; and 65535; and old,-65536; or disjoint; store i64 @off8; store i32 manh @off4; store i32 manl @off0; load x86_fp80 @0 (return u.e)`. analyzeStructure explicitly declines the non-fp80-seeded reload-pack (line ~231, "integer-seeded reload packs are a DISTINCT shape and stay declined" — same family as lroundl SET_LDBL).
   Re-running the SAME peephole on the clone body changes NOTHING: with a tainted arg these 6 would decline LOUDLY (kMsgFp80Padding) instead of silently. Covering them is NEW union-promotion coverage, not a re-run.

(3) Behind the unions, @expl carries 2 TAINTED-ACCUMULATOR polynomial-eval loops (__polevll Horner over const fp80 tables @P/@Q: `acc = fmuladd(acc, x*x, coeff[i])`, trip counts 2 and 3, `phi ptr [@P,..],[gep i8 %p,16,..]`, `llvm.loop` present — NOT unrolled at -O1). The accumulator phi %117 is tainted (x*x derives from the theta arg). Even with every union promoted, these decline: in-clone loop lowering is Phase 7.3 / 8h7d (static-K full-unroll) territory, and NEITHER lowerLoops NOR any unroll runs on a spec-clone body (specialize is after lowerLoops).

NET: the union is only the FIRST-declining layer. A Shadow-only increment would move expl shadow->loop and compile NO target cell (exactly the "advance the frontier but COMPILES unchanged" pattern I flagged for I2). And all 7 transcendental cells route through polynomial-eval inner callees (all transcendentals use Horner/__polevll loops), so this applies to all 7. The task done-criterion "coshl compiles at -O1" is NOT reachable via the Shadow lever alone; it needs union-coverage + in-clone static-K loop unroll + I2 control composed in one spec clone. Escalating to owner for scope decision (Shadow-coverage increment vs full 3-lever epic vs retarget to a leaf/straight-line cell such as lroundl/llroundl).

title: libm fp-ABI specialization: Phase-6 clone with fp (f16/f32/f64/f80) quantum arg/return — lift the i32-only FpAbi gate
description:

The 'fp-copy/specialization' bucket = 7 ld80 cells (atan2l, coshl, lgammal, log10l, powl, sinhl, tgammal) whose reduction calls an inner helper with an fp80 quantum ARG and/or RETURN. All decline CHAR-FOR-CHAR on: 'cq specialization: floating-point quantum argument or return has no reversible copy'.

ROOT CAUSE (IR-confirmed): SpecializeReject.cpp scanBody return gate (~line 235) requires RetW == "i32" EXACTLY -> SpecReject::FpAbi; the arg gate is the sibling. An fp80 (or f16/f32/f64) quantum arg/return is declined even though cqrt_copy_f{16,32,64,80} ALREADY EXIST in the runtime ABI (cq_runtime.h:285-288, bd 38t2) + cqrt_copy_f<W>_controlled (kjd1). BennettWrap.cpp:31 carries the sibling 'clone return width has no reversible copy' message. So this is a LARGELY-UNWIRED fence, NOT a physics wall (3c6m.50: zero C-physics walls on these cells).

FIX SHAPE (Rule-13 HIGH -- the fp-copy + angle boundary is the f64-angle miscompile family): (1) lift the FpAbi arg/return gate to admit the fp widths that HAVE a reversible copy (an fp-copy predicate over {f16,f32,f64,f80} -- mirror abiWidthHasControlledFpCopy / widthHasQramCell, NOT widthHasReversibleCopy whose fp-null IS the live f64-angle classifier); (2) BennettWrap copy-out via cqrt_copy_f<W> instead of cqrt_copy_i32; the clone's fp arg/return i32-HANDLE representation (a handle is always i32 regardless of the value's fp width -- Rule 15); (3) THE ANGLE-SAFETY FENCE (Rule 3, non-negotiable): the passed/returned fp must be provably DATA, never a rotation arg-1 angle -- mirror the kjd1 fp-select angle fence + declineTaintedAngle/taintedAngleGate; an fp arg used as an angle inside the callee still DECLINES. Coordinate with the vqlq value-bitcast carve (the int-sig+internal-union case, DONE) and 5po2 (tainted control in clones).

SCOPE: 7 ld80 cells + their f32/f64 SIBLINGS (coshf/cosh, atan2f/atan2, powf/pow, sinhf/sinh, tgammaf/tgamma, log10f/log10, lgammaf/lgamma) -- likely a dozen+ census cells across widths, so re-census f32/f64 too after landing (they may share the gate). NOTE it advances the 3c6m math.h epic's CELL coverage but is a DIFFERENT LEVER than 3c6m.51 (which is SHADOW / fp80-union bit-pattern memory); this is the Phase-6 specialization fp-ABI.

DONE CRITERIA: >=1 real e2e golden per newly-cleared cell (Rule 2/16), the FpAbi arg+return red-green fixtures (positive fp-arg/fp-return spec accept + the angle-fence decline mirrored char-for-char), independent Rule-13 clearance (fp-copy correctness + angle boundary), ctest green, no census regression. notes:

They ADVANCE one census layer -- the fp-ABI gate cleared, revealing the NEXT blocker: InBodyControl on the inner transcendental reduction the spec candidate calls (e.g. coshl -> expl x86_fp80(x86_fp80): 'callee contains tainted control flow under quantum lift' -- expl's overflow/underflow branches are multi-block, rejected by scanBody's single-block gate). title: Over-decline: const-folded straight-through edge blocks idiomatic 'if (x != 0) x = cq_phi(x, θ)' phase arm
description:
A tainted conditional PHASE written the most natural way — 'if (x != 0) x = cq_phi(x, θ); measure(x)' — is OVER-DECLINED ('control flow under quantum control'), even though it is a legitimate, coherent phase arm.

ROOT CAUSE (grounded in code): clang -O1 only reaches the else/straight-through edge when x==0, so it value-propagates the merge phi's Pred-edge incoming to the CONSTANT 0 (Rule 9: 'value-propagating the straight-through edge to a constant'). ArmClassify.cpp:788 requires the arm-spine base to equal the routed straight-through handle ('if (Routed && Base == Routed)'), but Routed is now the folded constant 0 while Base is the qubit handle -> Base != Routed -> falls through to decline. tryEqFoldArm handles a const-folded ARM GATE (q==k true arm folds to cq_phi(k,θ)) and the switch §5 const-fold re-anchor handles switch, but NOTHING re-anchors this const-folded diamond STRAIGHT-THROUGH (Pred) edge.

PROOF it is a real over-decline, not ambiguity:
  - 'if (b != 0) b = cq_phi(b,3.14)'  -> merge phi [phase(b), 0]  -> DECLINES.
  - 'if (b > 2)  b = cq_phi(b,3.14)'  -> else edge proves a RANGE (b<=2), clang keeps %3, merge phi [phase(b), %3] -> LOWERS CLEAN and runs end-to-end.
The only difference is whether clang could fold the else edge to a bare constant. Semantically phi[phase(b),0] == phi[phase(b),b] because on that edge x==0 is PROVEN by the branch, so re-anchoring Routed to the qubit is SOUND.

PROPOSED FIX: add a straight-through const-fold re-anchor in ArmClassify — when the Pred-edge incoming is a ConstantInt k that the branch condition PROVES equals the routed qubit's basis value on that edge (icmp eq %q, k on the Pred->merge edge), re-anchor Routed to %q. Analogous to the existing switch §5 re-anchor and tryEqFoldArm.

MUST NOT over-accept (Prime Directive / Rule 13): must NOT fire for demo/foo_superposition/foo.c, where the else constant 0 is NOT provably equal to the qubit on the else edge — the OR condition (b>4)||(b==0) does not prove b==0, and foo's (b<5)?b:0 makes the merge a genuine many-to-one value collapse mixed with a phase (correct decline). Ship red-green fixtures (positive CHECK for if(x!=0); negative 'RUN: not' for the OR-merge collapse) + adversarial Rule-13 review before commit.

REPRO: see demo/foo_superposition/. Also isolated single-file repros used during investigation:
  if (b != 0) b = cq_phi(b,0.5);  // declines (this bug)
  if (b > 2)  b = cq_phi(b,3.14); // lowers clean (control shape IS supported)

description: Follow-on from dugh (owner-directed defer, 2026-07-04). dugh accepts onward-QUANTUM arith/phase off a control-merge %out via the second propagation round, but a LOCAL-array store of the merged QUANTUM handle (arr[i]=y where y is %out a qubit handle) is NOT reachable by re-propagation: it is a store of a tainted value into memory (an escape). The Phase-7.5 Shadow model (Inc 2) only accepts arr[q]=classical_value (TAINTED index, CLASSICAL value) -- never storing a quantum HANDLE into a slot. BOTH flavors decline today: classical-index arr[i]=y -> kMsgStore; tainted-index arr[q]=y -> kMsgOther (the gep). Probe: scratchpad/8mld/pA1_localarray_store.ll (declines kMsgStore under dugh, valid input). FIX SHAPE: a g7ip-sibling store->load forwarding -- prove a scratch alloca slot is single-write/single-read/no-alias/no-escape at a definite (or provably-round-tripping) address, then RAUW the load to the stored SSA handle (%out) and erase the store/load, so measure(load) becomes measure(%out). Distinct mechanism from dugh's re-propagate; own PRD + Rule-13 clearance. Relates to g7ip (inline-the-producer) and 7.5 Shadow (QramLowering).
design: BLOCKED on owner scope decision (investigated 2026-07-04, owner asked but away). FINDING: the d3ji store->load forwarding accept-shape is UNREACHABLE on the clang -O1 validated floor -- clang GVN already forwards every provably-same-address, no-escape, single-write/single-read scratch round-trip BEFORE cq-lowering runs; d3ji's accept-set is a STRICT SUBSET of GVN's forward-set. A round-trip survives -O1 ONLY when the addresses are not provably equal, which is EXACTLY the case d3ji must decline (forwarding would silent-miscompile). Verified on 6 real -O1 emissions (scratchpad/d3ji/t*.c): same-index/struct/barrier/const-slots all forwarded away (measure reads the phi directly, dugh/6.5 lowers it -- no d3ji); only arr[i]=y;load arr[j] with two separate volatile-read indices survives, and that is a mandatory DECLINE. g7ip survives -O1 only because its store/load straddle a non-inlined CALL boundary; a same-function local array has no such barrier. CONSEQUENCE: a d3ji forwarder is dead on -O1 and cannot be gated by an e2e golden (Rule 16); the current kMsgStore decline is already CORRECT (safe over-decline on hand-authored off-floor IR only, no real input mishandled). RECOMMENDATION: close as not-reachable/won't-fix, keep the safe decline, do NOT add unexercisable mutation code to the correctness-critical core. ALT: rescope to a quantum handle read back at a QUANTUM index (superposition register-file, dual of 7.5 Shadow, no-cloning-bound) -- a different capability, not forwarding. Full analysis: docs/prd/phase-04-swap-route-control/d3ji-scratch-store-forward-PRD.md + bd memories d3ji-gvn-subsumption-finding. NO code changed; safe decline + fixture untouched.
close_reason: Not-reachable / won't-fix (owner-approved 2026-07-04). The current kMsgStore decline is the correct safe over-decline (fires only on hand-authored off-floor IR; no real input mishandled). No core change; safe decline + fixture kept.
