title: Non-i32 quantum returns: carry an i32 handle out of an iN-typed return (project-wide)
description:
Accept-everything-physics-allows follow-on discovered during 8mld (owner decision 2026-07-03: decline now, file feature).

PROBLEM. Returning a quantum value at a width other than i32 is PHYSICS-VALID (a 64-bit quantum register is fine) but currently DECLINES project-wide, because runtime handles are ALWAYS i32 (cqrt_alloc_<W> returns i32 at every width — the frozen ABI, Rule 15). `ret iN <i32 handle>` is a type mismatch -> broken module. The taint-escape guard (TaintPropagation.cpp declineTaintEscapes, kMsgNonI32Return) already declines every non-i32 tainted return: value diamonds, phase diamonds, straight-line theta (pinned rejects lowering_reject_taint_escape_return_{value,phase}_diamond.ll). 8mld extends the same decline to the two UNTAINTED-merge paths (classical-call arm, switch data-mux) which previously SIGABRTd instead of declining.

SO the non-i32 quantum RETURN is the one shape that is "physics allows but we do not lower" — an ABI/representation limit, NOT physics. This bead is to lift it.

FIX SHAPE (project-wide, NOT specific to any one control path). To return a quantum value from an iN-typed function: carry the i32 handle out (e.g. zext the handle to iN, or change the quantum-returning clone signature to i32) AND teach the Phase-6 caller-side clone machinery (__cq_q_<name>_<mask>) to RECOVER the handle on the caller side (trunc/bitcast back to an i32 handle before further quantum use). Today the clone machinery assumes i32 quantum returns only. Touches EVERY return path (escape guard + FreePoint Escaped case + clone lifting), so it is a cross-cutting change, not an 8mld gate.

BOUNDARY. i32 quantum returns already work (the caller owns the i32 handle). Measurement at any width already works (the sink re-types). This is purely about the RAW (unmeasured) return at width != i32.

REQUIRES: own PRD + Rule-13 clearance. Relates to [[re-propagate-untainted-control-merge]] (dugh) — both are "accept more physics" follow-ons from 8mld.
notes: DEFERRED 2026-07-09: libm-campaign pivot (owner) — orthogonal to the 6-lever plan; resurrect on demand if a census decline names this shape. See bd memory libm-campaign-pivot.

title: Re-propagate the untainted control-merge %out so onward quantum flow lowers (not declines)
description:
Accept-everything-physics-allows follow-on discovered during 8mld (owner-directed, 2026-07-03).

PROBLEM. A tainted-condition control region can produce a merge value that is DATA-untainted yet QUANTUM-by-control-dependence: e.g. `int y=5; if(q>3) y=f(a);` — y is the superposition {f(a) on q>3, 5 on q<=3}, entangled with q. The 4.5 switch data-mux and 6.5 classical-call arm emitters build that superposition register %out and DO tag it taint.Tainted, but they run AFTER `propagate` (data-flow taint from cq_theta) has already classified the DOWNSTREAM consumers as classical, and there is NO second propagation round. So `z = y + 1; measure z;`, `cq_phi(y,θ)`, and a LOCAL-array (QRAM/Shadow) store `arr[i]=y` — all physics-valid quantum-onward flows — are left reading %out (an i32 qubit handle) as if it were a value. Pre-8mld these silently leaked / late-rejected / SIGABRTd; 8mld now DECLINES them uniformly ("control flow under quantum control") as a SAFE INTERIM (over-decline, Prime Directive). This bead is to ACCEPT them.

WHY IT DECLINES (root): taint tracks DATA-flow, not CONTROL-dependence. The control emitter is the thing that knows the merge is quantum, but it fires after propagate/escape/lowerOps and does not re-run them. Confirmed by probe (scratchpad/8mld/pA_arith_measure.ll, pA_phi_measure.ll, pA1_localarray_store.ll — all DECLINE today, all valid input verify exit 0).

FIX SHAPE. After control emit, run a SECOND propagation round seeded from the control-owned rails (taint.ControlOwnedRails / the %out allocs): (1) re-propagate taint forward from %out; (2) re-run the escape guards (declineTaintEscapes) so onward CLASSICAL escapes (opaque-ptr store / opaque call / non-i32 ret) still decline via the existing net; (3) let lowerOps/lowerMeasures/uncompute pick up the newly-tainted onward ops. Must handle interaction with the flattened CFG, FreePoint, and the whole-DAG uncompute (the new tainted DAG). This is the roadmap "quantum data under quantum control flows onward" (Phase 4x6) capability.

SCOPE BOUNDARY. This never changes an (A1) decline: opaque/classical-pointer store, opaque classical call, and non-i32 raw return stay declined (physics/ABI-forced). This only converts the (A2) subset (onward QUANTUM flow: arith/phase/local-array-store that stays quantum until an eventual measure or i32-ret) from decline to accept.

REQUIRES: own PRD + Rule-13 clearance (core-lowering, second propagation round). Both untainted-merge producers (classical-call arm, switch data-mux) share the fix.
notes: DONE + Rule-13 CLEARED 2026-07-04 (branch dugh-repropagate-control-merge, commit 67a40eb). Second-propagation round (repropagateControlMerges) re-seeds taint from taint.UntaintedMergeRails after control emit; retires the 8mld merge-out gates. ACCEPT (A2): onward arith/phase (incl. under a classical if via 5j5 lift) -> measure/i32-ret. DECLINE: onward classical escape, new tainted control on %out, tainted angle, frozen-plan call (spec/by-ref-math), quantum-handle store. 3 latent Rule-13 defects found+fixed across 3 adversarial rounds (2->1->0 confirmed): D1 flatten <badref> SIGSEGV (replaceSuccessorsPhiUsesWith x3), D2 spec-clone handle-as-literal miscompile, D3 by-ref-math broken module (D2+D3: declineReseedIntoFrozenPlan). Also fixed declineTaintEscapes case-4 to key on the function return type (post-RAUW 8mld broken module). Full ctest 63/63; 138-probe sweep clean. Local-array store of a quantum handle deferred to d3ji. See memory dugh-second-propagation-round.

title: 6.5 classical-call arm: NON-i32 (i64) untainted merge phi SIGABRTs on ret iN (no width gate) instead of declining
description:
Found by the 4i7r Rule-13 adversarial clearance (over-accept-taintmiss lens), CONFIRMED (independent verify agent reproduced exit 134). ORTHOGONAL to 4i7r (no freeze involved); same CLASS — a taint-gated guard misses an UNTAINTED non-i32 quantum-controlled value that is then RAUW'd to an i32 handle — but the crash vehicle is 'ret', via the Phase 6.5 classical-call-under-quantum-control arm, not 'freeze'.

REPRO (well-formed valid IR; opt -passes=verify exit 0, llvm-as exit 0): the exact 6.5 accept shape 'int64_t y=5; if(q>3) y=f(a); return y;' where f is memory(none)/willreturn/nounwind (a pure classical call under quantum control) at i64 width. Probe: scratchpad/4i7r/ccarm_i64_ret_repro.ll (= review w0_ccarm_i64_ret_nofreeze.ll). Running the pass: SIGABRT 134 'Function return type does not match operand type of return inst! i64' -> 'Broken module found'. A crash on valid input violates Rule 1 (decline-loudly-or-lower).

ROOT CAUSE: classifyClassicalCallArm (ArmClassify.cpp:~1102-1213) has NO i32-width gate on the merge phi. The only width check is the emitter's copyControlledFn(Abi) non-null test (ClassicalCallArmEmit.cpp:~107-113), which IS non-null for the i64 integer ABI (cqrt_copy_i64_controlled exists), so i64 sails through. emitClassicalCallArmRegion RAUWs the i64 merge phi to an i32 cqrt_alloc_i64 handle, leaving 'ret i64 %out(i32)'. declineTaintEscapes' non-i32-return guard (TaintPropagation.cpp:~692) is TAINT-GATED (taint.Tainted.count(RV)) and this merge is UNTAINTED (constant straight-through 5 + classical-call result), so it slips past.

WIDTH-SPECIFICITY / ORTHOGONALITY confirmed by controls: the i32-width variant lowers clean (exit 0); the i64 MEASURE-sink variant lowers clean (measure re-types the result to the classical value); the sibling SWITCH data-mux at i64 correctly LOUD-DECLINES ('control flow under quantum control'). So the classical-call arm is the unguarded outlier. SECONDARY: adding a freeze over the merge (v1_ccarm_i64_freeze_ret.ll) MASKS the crash to a SILENT exit-0 broken module (LLVM verifier gap: a FreezeInst with operand-type != result-type passes verify when dead/certain) — worse than the crash.

CANDIDATE FIX (Prime Directive, decline-safe): add a merge-phi width gate in classifyClassicalCallArm mirroring the switch data-mux / controlled-IO i32 restriction — require MergePhi->getType()->isIntegerTy(32), loud-decline otherwise (over-declines the rare i64 measured case, which is safe). Red-green negative fixture mirroring the diagnostic char-for-char. Core-lowering change -> needs its own Rule-13 clearance.

BROADER AUDIT NOTE (from the reviewer): this is one instance of a root pattern — ANY non-i32 quantum-controlled value RAUW'd to an i32 handle then consumed by a NON-measure user (ret/store/opaque) crashes. Audit SelectMergeEmit and the value-arm merge paths for the same ret-escape blind spot.
notes:
RESOLUTION (2026-07-03, owner-directed decline approach). Fix = a G6-mirror MERGE-OUT ESCAPE GATE (per-consumer walk), NOT the notes candidate blanket isIntegerTy(32) gate. Rationale: the blanket gate would (a) OVER-DECLINE the working i64-MEASURE case, and (b) NOT fix the leak (store/opaque at i32 stays a leak under a mere width gate). The surgical walk requires every MergePhi->users() to be a measure sink (any width -- re-types) OR a ret at i32; else loud decline. Preserves i64-measure on BOTH paths (verified end-to-end: cqrt_measure_i64(i32 %out), module clean).

TWO ADVERSARIAL CORRECTIONS to the original note (Rule 11 skepticism, both reproduced): (1) the note claimed "the sibling SWITCH data-mux at i64 correctly LOUD-DECLINES" -- FALSE. switch(q){...}->phi i64->ret i64 ALSO SIGABRTs (proveSwitchDataMux G6 allowed ret at ANY width). Fixed the switch too (G6 ret-branch gated to i32). (2) the note did not mention that the classical-call arm ALSO SILENTLY LEAKS the %out handle when the merge is consumed by a store/opaque-call/arith at ANY width (it had NO consumer gate). Fixed by the same walk. So 8mld was 3 manifestations of one root (untainted-merge escape), all fixed; see memory untainted-merge-escape-8mld.

VERIFIED: 9-probe baseline->fixed battery correct; full ctest 62/62; 5 red-green fixtures. RULE-13 CLEARED (4 independent lenses, 51 probes, 0 defects, untainted-merge class confirmed fully closed).

DECLINE SCOPE (owner-agreed): (A1) opaque-ptr store / opaque classical call / non-i32 raw return = physics/ABI FORCED decline. (A2) onward QUANTUM flow (arith/phase/local-array QRAM store on the merged value) = physics-VALID, declines only because the untainted merge is not re-propagated -> FILED as features dugh (re-propagate control-merge) + jx32 (non-i32 quantum returns). 8mld itself is the crash+leak->decline fix.

title: coverage: split LOWERING vs BACKEND coverage — tiered backend column (standard/synthesizable/open)
description: The library coverage table (tools/library_coverage/) has ONE axis today and 'golden-verified' conflates two levels. title: Broaden the in-place arithmetic strategy beyond loop-rail self-update (global liveness dispatch + two-quantum adder)
description:
Follow-on to dtzb (the in-place reversible arithmetic strategy). dtzb intentionally scoped the in-place add/xor to a recognized loop-carried RAIL SELF-UPDATE only (owner decision 2026-06-26: minimal blast radius, NO straight-line golden churn). This issue tracks BROADENING the in-place strategy across the codebase — the deferred axes (each was an explicit follow-on from the dtzb scope AskUserQuestion):

AXIS 1 — GLOBAL in-place dispatch (liveness-based). Lower ANY tainted value self-update whose old operand is DEAD in place (q = q OP c with q dead after), not just loop rails — including straight-line code. Matches Bennett.jl's general dispatch (in-place when the result overwrites a DYING operand; out-of-place when a live operand must survive). Reduces qubit count broadly. COST: flips existing straight-line goldens where an operand happens to be dead (e.g. slice_theta_add_measure: y = x + 1 with x dead -> in-place addc) -> DELIBERATE baseline regeneration (Rule 12) + wider Rule-13 review. Needs a precise liveness/aliasing dispatch predicate (single-use of the dying operand; no escape/alias).

AXIS 2 — TWO-QUANTUM in-place adder (acc = acc + q, BOTH operands quantum). The general in-place Cuccaro adder: acc <- acc + q over a LIVE quantum operand q (q preserved), Bennett.jl's lower_add_cuccaro! ((a,b)->(a,a+b)). Currently the X1 two-quantum decline rejects it (lowering_reject_loop_value_accum_two_quantum.ll). An in-place two-operand adder makes acc += q accumulator loops rolled-lowerable in place (dynamic-K), SUPERSEDING the static-K unroll fallback (799w.3 / rkg1) for the accumulate case. Needs a two-quantum in-place ABI (e.g. cqrt_add_<W> handle+handle in-place) — DISTINCT from dtzb's classical-immediate addc/xorc.

AXIS 3 (optional) — more in-place bijections: sub (foldable into addc with a negated immediate), mul-by-ODD-constant (invertible mod 2^W), constant shifts/rotates (barrel). Each a reversible bijection with a clean in-place form; each a new in-place ABI symbol family.

Decline-safe today (the un-broadened shapes ride the existing out-of-place / X1 / decline paths — no correctness gap, only a qubit-count/expressiveness gap). Each axis ships red-green fixtures + independent Rule-13 review (core arithmetic/loop change; the dtzb review already found a fan-out silent miscompile in this area — see loop-rail-inplace-fanout-miscompile). Supersedes 799w.3 / rkg1 for the self-update (done, dtzb) + accumulate (axis 2) subcases. See bd memory 7.4-inplace-arith-strategy-unblocker.
acceptance_criteria: Global liveness-based in-place dispatch for straight-line self-updates (deliberate golden regen) AND a two-quantum in-place Cuccaro adder for acc+=q accumulate loops (dynamic-K, superseding 799w.3/rkg1 for that case); each axis red-green + Rule-13 cleared.

title: ControlDetect emits BROKEN MODULE for a tainted control region inside a loop body (should loud-decline)
description:
PRE-EXISTING robustness/correctness bug found by the dtzb Rule-13 adversarial review (2026-06-26), confirmed OUT OF dtzb scope (reproduces on a pure rotation rail where no dtzb value path runs). A tainted control region (an if-diamond) INSIDE a classically-bounded loop body makes the pass emit a BROKEN MODULE — invalid IR — instead of either lowering correctly or LOUD-declining (Prime Directive / Rule 1: an unprovable shape must decline loudly, NEVER emit invalid IR).

SYMPTOM (verify failure, opt exit=1, but NOT a DiagnosticInfoUnsupported decline):
  PHI node entries do not match predecessors!
    %i = phi i32 [ 0, %entry ], [ %in, %loop ]
ControlDetect recognizes the in-loop tainted diamond (here an empty-arm identity region, `if(qn==0){}`) and RegionFlatten flattens it, but the flatten merges/erases blocks WITHOUT fixing the enclosing loop's induction-phi predecessor structure -> the loop header phi's incoming-block list no longer matches its actual predecessors -> invalid module. tryCaseA returns false at the L2 tainted-control-in-body check (7.3 does not lower control-in-loop), leaving the region to ControlDetect, which has no in-loop guard.

NOT a silent miscompile (the verifier catches it, so opt exits non-zero), but a real robustness gap: a tainted control region inside a loop must be detected and LOUD-declined BEFORE flattening (the loop CFG interaction is unproven), not flattened into invalid IR. Likely low clang-reachability (an empty-arm `if(c){}` in a loop is often eliminated by -O1; a non-empty-arm `if(c) q=cq_phi(q,..)` in a loop declines cleanly today via the taint-escape / classical-mux guard), so this is the hand-written / off-pattern surface — but the pass must be robust on valid input.

MINIMAL REPRO (pA_rot.ll — pure rotation rail, no dtzb):
  declare double @cq_theta_f64(double, double)
  declare double @cq_phi_f64(double, double)
  declare double @cq_measure_f64(double)
  define double @cmprot(double %seed, i32 %n) {
  entry:
    %q0 = call double @cq_theta_f64(double %seed, double 2.500000e-01)
    %g = icmp sgt i32 %n, 0
    br i1 %g, label %loop, label %exit
  loop:
    %i = phi i32 [0,%entry],[%in,%loop]
    %q = phi double [%q0,%entry],[%qn,%loop]
    %qn = call double @cq_phi_f64(double %q, double 1.250000e-01)
    %c = fcmp oeq double %qn, 0.0
    br i1 %c, label %side, label %cont
  side:
    br label %cont
  cont:
    %in = add nuw nsw i32 %i, 1
    %d = icmp eq i32 %in, %n
    br i1 %d, label %exit, label %loop
  exit:
    %a = phi double [%q0,%entry],[%qn,%cont]
    %m = call double @cq_measure_f64(double %a)
    ret double %m
  }
Run: opt -load-pass-plugin build/ir-pass/libCQPass.so -passes=cq-lowering -S pA_rot.ll  => "PHI node entries do not match predecessors!". (The compare/value twin pA_cmp.ll reproduces identically.)

FIX DIRECTION: ControlDetect (or RegionFlatten) must detect that a candidate tainted control region's blocks lie inside a natural loop (LoopInfo) and LOUD-decline it ("... under quantum control") rather than flatten — OR fix the flatten to repair the enclosing loop's phi predecessors. Decline is the safe v1 (over-declining is safe; control-in-loop is the 7.3 L2 deferral anyway). Ship with a mirror-exact decline fixture + the pA_rot/pA_cmp probes as regression pins (Rule 12). Rule-13 (touches the control/flatten core).
acceptance_criteria: A tainted control region whose blocks lie inside a natural loop is LOUD-declined (DiagnosticInfoUnsupported, opt exits non-zero) BEFORE any flatten; the pA_rot.ll/pA_cmp.ll repros no longer produce invalid IR; mirror-exact decline fixture + regression pins; Rule-13 cleared (control/flatten core).
close_reason: VERIFIED FALSE ALARM — closed-as-not-a-bug (owner decision 2026-06-30). The 'broken module' symptom is opt's INPUT verifier rejecting the issue's MALFORMED hand-written repro (pA_rot.ll): its loop header phis read 'phi i32 [0,entry],[%in,%loop]' but the real backedge predecessor is %cont — opt rejects this before the pass runs, and that input-verifier text EXACTLY matches the pasted symptom. The pass itself never emitted invalid IR. With the backedge corrected (->%cont), the pass declines CLEANLY; verified across 5 diverse valid in-loop tainted-control shapes (empty-arm; flat phase-arm diamond at latch / mid-block / pred-not-header; depth-2 nested; i32 + f64) — every one loud-declines, NONE break. ControlDetect/RegionFlatten unchanged since the issue. In-loop control is already handled (nested: recoverRegionTree backedge guard 'nested control flow'; flat: structural decline + declineClassicalMuxes). No code change. Full finding in bd memory fch8-inloop-control-false-alarm. A built explicit detect-before-flatten guard (declines all 5 with an accurate message) was NOT shipped — partly redundant + changes the nested fixture message; owner chose close-as-false-alarm. The one real-but-minor item (in-loop quantum-condition control reports the misleading 'classical-condition phi' diagnostic) is split out as d8jl (P3, diagnostic-accuracy only).

title: BUG (residual): local QRAM array leaks stores when a loaded value escapes INDIRECTLY (arith-then-return / fan-out)
description: Follow-up to sxuk (fixed in commit 3abdaa0, the DIRECT case). title: Phase 7.1 follow-up — i128 wide-int support (FROZEN ABI · aggregate-source ABI design · pre-freeze)
description: Deferred from Increment D 2026-06-20 (owner). The IMPLEMENTATION-PLAN-7.1 §6 i128 mechanism is empirically FALSE on clang 19.1.7 / x86_64 (darwin AND linux): a C __int128/unsigned __int128 function param+return is decomposed by the C ABI into {i64,i64} aggregates (cq_theta_si128 emits as '{i64,i64} @cq_theta_si128(i64,i64,double)'), so abiWidthFromType (expects 128-bit IntegerType) and declMatchesPrototype (expects i128 source) never recognize it; a tainted 'add i128' on a small constant is split into add-i128-low + add-i64-high threaded by extractvalue/zext/trunc/lshr; cq_measure_si128 takes 2 i64 args; and -O1 demanded-bits eliminates i128 intermediates entirely. See memory 7-1-D-i128-abi-shred. MUST land before Phase-11 freeze (adds frozen symbols). DESIGN MUST SOLVE: (1) recognize the {i64,i64} aggregate cq_theta/measure ABI as a single logical i128 source/sink (aggregate taint seeding through extractvalue); (2) coalesce clang's split i128-low + i64-high arithmetic back into a logical i128 op, or lower the split form faithfully; (3) the 2-arg measure ABI. Alternatively reconsider the i128 frontend source representation. This is a real sub-project, NOT Increment-D-sized. ACCEPTANCE: i128 frozen symbol family in opcode_table.yaml + cqrt_* core ABI; e2e golden round-trips a >64-bit value with no truncation; independent Rule-13 clearance; lands before freeze. Parent epic test_C_libtooling-sbt1.
close_reason: Tier-1 (i128 INTERMEDIATE) DONE + Rule-13 cleared 2026-06-21. i128 lowers as a recognized intermediate width (+215 frozen symbols, 1732->1947, no cqrt_*_i128 core); source/sink (__int128 {i64,i64} shred) is Tier-2, deferred post-freeze (blocked at CQ.h _Generic + the unrecognized-suffix passthrough boundary). 5 fence groups (widthHasReversibleCopy + control gates, copyFn/copyControlledFn>64, dataTemplateFn guard, castInScope cross-domain, CompareLowering+scanBody icmp). Design doc DESIGN-i128-n0ui.md; memory n0ui-i128-tier1-implemented. ctest 34/34, drift 0. Tier-2 filed as a separate post-freeze follow-up.

title: Phase 7.1 follow-up D5 — _BitInt(N) round-up + visible high-bit mask (FROZEN ABI · OUT of 7.1, pre-freeze)
description: Plan §6 D5 / §9 (owner decision 2026-06-20): tracked pre-freeze follow-up, NOT part of 7.1 Increment D. Within 7.1, _BitInt(N) for non-ABI N PERMANENTLY DECLINES (abiWidthFromType empty -> loud 'no template'); the decline fixture lowering_reject_bitint_intermediate_unmasked.ll (add i40 -> no template) is a STANDING decline for 7.1, the regression anchor this follow-up later converts. Must land BEFORE the Phase-11 freeze since it adds FROZEN symbols. Support a non-power-of-2 _BitInt(N) as an INTERMEDIATE (mid-computation via cast/arith) by lowering via the next ABI width + masking high bits to preserve wraparound/overflow semantics (add nsw on logical i24 != on i32 — the mask is LOAD-BEARING correctness, an unmasked round-up is a verify-clean overflow miscompile).
design: What the follow-up must ship: (1) a NEW frozen masked-op family enumerated in opcode_table.yaml (own rows, abi_codegen shape, WIDTH_INFO, a COUNT DELTA in gen_templates_test) — e.g. cq_template_mask_<W>_hl(handle, lit=2^N-1); (2) the mask as a VISIBLE IR-level reversible op inserted in ArithLowering AFTER the arith template call and BEFORE the RAUW — it CANNOT hide in the trace-only runtime body (cq_templates.c does zero arithmetic); (3) the literal EXACTLY 2^N-1 (2^N / 2^(N-1) is itself a miscompile, Rule 10); (4) the mask op PARTICIPATES in the whole-DAG _unc reversal (cq_template_-prefixed so EmitInverse:128-147 handles it — but PROVE the _unc shape is correct for a masking op) + an _unc-shape fixture; (5) Rule-13 analytic proof that no unmasked path exists, then FLIP the standing decline fixture to a positive lowering_bitint_intermediate_masked_i40.ll.
acceptance_criteria: Standing 7.1 decline lowering_reject_bitint_intermediate_unmasked.ll FLIPPED to positive lowering_bitint_intermediate_masked_i40.ll; new frozen cq_template_mask_<W> family in opcode_table.yaml + regen (--check 0, count delta in gen_templates_test); visible mask op in ArithLowering between template-call and RAUW; literal exactly 2^N-1; mask op reversed in whole-DAG _unc + _unc-shape fixture; e2e golden round-trips a _BitInt(N) round+mask; independent Rule-13 clearance (no unmasked path) before commit; lands before Phase-11 freeze.
close_reason: RESOLVED 2026-06-21 by REFRAME (no new frozen ABI, owner-approved). Real clang -O1 codegen (Rule 11) disproved the premise: clang rounds _BitInt(N<=64) to the ABI width and emits the wraparound as a stock and/shl/ashr, which already lower via existing frozen templates -- _BitInt(N<=64) already round-trips end-to-end (signed+unsigned, verify-clean, e2e golden). The cq_template_mask_<W> family is unnecessary; removes m0yi from the freeze-gating set. Shipped: 3 lit fixtures (unsigned+and-mask _unc, signed shl/ashr, trunc-to-i40 safety-net decline) + e2e-slice-bitint golden + plan D5 SUPERSEDED annotation + memory bitint-already-lowers-clang-rounds-and-masks. ctest 33/33, drift 0, ZERO frozen symbols / pass-code unchanged.

title: Phase 7.1 Increment C — N-ary classical-condition merge-phi lift (no ABI)
description: Plan §5. Pure analysis change; NO symbols. The whole correctness payload is the per-edge conditional-execution proof generalized to ALL other edges, not the 2-way 1-i complement. Reuse (already arity-agnostic): resolveWireBase, terminatorIsClassical (accepts classical switch), the idom-terminator check, the LiftedConsumers re-sweep, scrubTaint. FP-vs-data guard preserved verbatim (isFPOrFPVectorTy — N-ary widens arity, not FP/data classification).
design: Single load-bearing edit (TaintPropagation.cpp): :635 -> N=getNumIncomingValues(); if(N<2) return false. :646-649 -> SmallVector<WireChain,4> over incoming_values(); require every Chains[k].Base==Chains[0].Base AND Chains[0].Base!=Phi. :667-670 pred-terminator loop [0,N). :677-701 CORE -> drop Chains[2]/Other=getIncomingBlock(1-i); per edge i, per gate G in Chains[i].Gates: keep (6) G->getParent()!=Self->false, keep (7b) isPotentiallyReachable(Self->getTerminator(),G)->false, GENERALIZE (7a) to ALL other edges: for j in [0,N), j!=i: if isPotentiallyReachable(G, IncomingBlock(j)->getTerminator(), nullptr, &*DT) return false. ACCEPT tail unchanged -> RAUW to Chains[0].Base. INVARIANT: build all N WireChains and complete every proof BEFORE any mutation (pure-analysis until ACCEPT tail; partial-mutation-then-bail corrupts the module). N==2 must reduce EXACTLY to the prior 1-i logic. Do NOT touch the SelectInst branch (:766-776 — a select's gate dominates it; lifting turns 'rotate iff c' into 'always rotate').

VERIFY every pre-existing arity-2 fixture behaviorally unchanged; SelectInst branch untouched. e2e: tests/e2e/slice_classical_switch_gate.c (switch from argc, un-foldable, in-place cq_phi arms on one register, measure; golden shows only executed arm's cqrt_rz). title: Q/C boundary: out-of-scope fcmp predicate (one/ueq/ord/uno/...) silently mints a non-existent template symbol (verify-clean miscompile)
description:
DISCOVERED during ziov.4 Rule-13 adversarial review (2026-06-15), confirmed by repro. A tainted data-position fcmp with an OUT-OF-SCOPE predicate (anything outside {oeq,une,olt,ogt,ole,oge} — i.e. one/ord/uno/ueq/ugt/uge/ult/ule/true/false) is lowered with NO scope check: CompareLowering::lowerCompareImpl computes the predicate name and width, then WidthDispatch::compareTemplateFn does an unconditional getOrInsertFunction(compareName(...)) which is NEVER null. There is no predicate-scope gate anywhere in the pass (no compareInScope analogous to castInScope; TaintPropagation/OpcodeLowering collect every tainted CmpInst regardless of predicate). 

RESULT: the pass emits a call to a runtime template that DOES NOT EXIST (the YAML ships only 6 fcmp preds — tools/opcode_table.yaml:83 'fcmp: [oeq, une, olt, ogt, ole, oge]'; runtime/cq_templates.c has only those). opt exits 0, opt -verify is clean, and the program fails at Stage-3 LINK with an undefined symbol — a verify-clean miscompile (the project's unforgivable class, Rule 1 fail-loud violated).

CONFIRMED REPROS (exit 0, bogus symbol minted):
1. STRAIGHT-LINE (no control flow, pre-existing & independent of ziov.4): 
   %a = call float @cq_theta_f32(float 2.0, double 0.5); %c = fcmp one float %a, 1.0; %m = call i1 @cq_measure_i1(i1 %c)
   -> mints 'call i32 @cq_template_fcmp_one_f32_hl(i32 %h, float 1.0)', exit 0, NO diagnostic.
2. COND-DATA-USE LINEAGE (mutate-then-fail; the ziov.4 detect-before-mutate family, NOT closed by ziov.4's cast-only gate): 
   %c=icmp sgt %q,5; %f=uitofp i1 %c to float (IN SCOPE); %g=fcmp one float %f,0.0 (OUT OF SCOPE); br %c ...
   -> condDataUseDisposition walks %c->%f(cast,ok)->%g(CmpInst, NO pred gate)->ShareOk; emitRegion ROUTES (cqrt_cswap emitted) + flattenRegion erases the diamond, THEN mints the bogus fcmp symbol. exit 0.

REACHABILITY: clang -O1 emits oeq/une/olt/ogt/ole/oge for C float ==,!=,<,>,<=,>= (all in scope). The out-of-scope preds arise from __builtin_isunordered, NaN-aware idioms (a<b||a>b -> one), or non-default fast-math. Uncommon but not synthetic-only; the project rule is decline-loud-never-silent regardless of frequency (Prime Directive).

FIX (recommended, mirrors castInScope): add compareInScope(StringRef op, StringRef predName, StringRef width) to OpcodeSupport (icmp: all 10 preds; fcmp: {oeq,une,olt,ogt,ole,oge}). Consult it in (a) CompareLowering::lowerCompareImpl/rewriteCompare -> diagnoseNoTemplate + return null (loud, leaves cmp standing, verify-clean) for the STRAIGHT-LINE root; and (b) ArmClassify::condDataUseDisposition CmpInst branch -> return CondDataDisp::Unlowerable for the cond-data-use DETECT-BEFORE-MUTATE half. Core lowering change -> Rule-13 adversarial review + red-green decline fixtures (straight-line negative + cond-data-use negative).
close_reason: compareInScope(op,pred) predicate-scope gate added to OpcodeSupport; consulted at 4 sites — CompareLowering::lowerCompareImpl (universal silent-mint backstop, fwd/_inv/QQ/HL), condDataUseDisposition CmpInst branch, classifyArms flat control cond, recoverRegionTree nested outer+inner. Out-of-scope fcmp now declines LOUDLY pre-mutation instead of minting a non-existent symbol. Rule-13 cleared by independent review (verified empirically). 4 red-green fixtures. icmp unaffected (all 10 in scope).

title: Pre-existing: dead arm-local cq_phi on a mux base lowers to an unbalanced in-arm controlled Rz
description:
ADVERSARIAL-REVIEW FINDING (u5f review, 2026-06-03), PRE-EXISTING (byte-identical old-vs-new — NOT introduced by u5f's G2/G3 widening). In a distinct-base MUX-EXCH gated switch, a DEAD arm-local cq_phi applied to a mux base q (a gate body in q's selecting arm whose RESULT is not what the mux φ edge carries) is collected into the arm's Gate shadow and lowered by substituteArm to an in-arm cqrt_rz_<W>_controlled(f_q, q, angle). The npu.6/u5f uncompute (emitChainInv) inverts only the UNCONDITIONAL prep chain (2-arg cqrt_ry/cqrt_rz with arg0==q), NOT this 3-arg controlled in-arm Rz — so on the SELECTED path q carries an extra Rz that the cswap moves into regOut (intended for real gate bodies) but if the cq_phi result is DEAD (not the φ-carried value) the Rz is stray, leaving regOut with an uncompensated rotation. G3b (per-arm correspondence) checks that a gate on q lives in a q-SELECTING arm but does NOT check that the gate's result is actually THREADED to the merge φ (vs a dead local). Needs its own adversarial review to (a) confirm reproducibility on a concrete fixture and (b) decide fix: tighten G3b to require the gate body's result reach the mux φ edge (resolveGatedHandleBase of the φ incoming == the gate, not just == its base), OR decline a mux arm containing a dead base-mutating gate. Probe label 'p2' in the u5f review. Over-decline is always safe. See docs/npu6-mux-exch-gate-spec.md §3 (G3a/G3b) + [[mux-exch-gate-per-arm-correspondence]].

## Context
Surfaced while implementing u5f (G2/G3 multi-op Bennett uncompute). Reviewer classified it pre-existing and out-of-scope for u5f; filed for a future hardening pass, mirroring how the shared-merge UAF (ehf) was split out of 5bl.
notes: RESOLVED — NOT A BUG (investigated 2026-06-03, empirical + independent adversarial verification). The hazard requires NON-LINEAR handle use (a no-cloning violation): a 'dead' cq_phi on mux base q whose result is not threaded to the φ needs q used twice off the same SSA value, which a well-formed linear program (CQ.h frontend; a truly dead/leaked handle is itself a linearity violation) cannot produce. Empirically a non-linear dead-clone arm lowers BYTE-IDENTICALLY to the well-formed linear two-gate arm (in-place handle model RAUWs {q, cq_phi(q,.), .} to one handle, so both cq_phi become two cqrt_rz on the one register = the valid linear interpretation; the 'extra' Rz is only extra under the non-physical cloning reading). The cswap captures all in-arm gates before the move and the non-selected uncompute IS balanced. Adversarial verifier (10 probe categories: linear chains, shared/folded arms, cross-block preps, default/direct-default, chained-theta+gate, measure/return escapes, crash sweep) found ZERO accepted-and-miscompiled inputs; every genuine cross-arm hazard is over-declined by G3b (_wrongarmmut*) and every cross-φ/post-merge cloning hazard by G6 (_crossphi_alias, _postmergelive). NOTE: a general IR-level no-cloning/linearity CHECKER is out of scope by design — the spec §1 establishes correctness by-construction on linear well-formed input, with the frontend guaranteeing linearity and specific cloning shapes declined (G6). Locked the well-formed sibling shape with lowering_control_switch_gated_distinct_multigatearm.ll.
close_reason: Closed

notes:
SPIKE FINDINGS (2026-06-03). PREREQUISITE BLOCKER: uncomputing a source's cq_theta (Ry) prep needs cqrt_ry_<W>_controlled_inv — the runtime has ONLY cqrt_rz_<W>_controlled_inv. Add 7 widths (i1/i8/i16/i32/i64/f32/f64) in runtime/cq_runtime.{h,c} + a ControlledSymbols accessor (mirror controlledRotationFn) FIRST. PLAN (direct-cq_theta case): for each base handle q, uncompute its prep on the branches where q is NON-selected — controlled on ¬f_q (= OR of the OTHER handles' selection flags) — by emitting cqrt_ry_<W>_controlled_inv(¬f_q, q, angle). Recover <angle> from the already-lowered cqrt_ry call on q (rotation lowering runs BEFORE controlled lowering, so the cq_theta is gone — scan for the cqrt_ry whose handle is q). GENERAL CASE (the 'spike it' part, UNSOLVED): a source with a multi-op prep history, a chained theta, or live out-of-region uses can't be naively reversed (Bennett/QROM-MUX-EXCH). TIGHTLY GATE: only lower when every base handle is a single direct cqrt_ry prep with no out-of-region uses; else decline (npu.1 path) — over-decline-safe. CANNOT be correctness-validated in the trace-only runtime (structural fixtures only).
GATE SPEC WRITTEN: docs/npu6-mux-exch-gate-spec.md (adversarial design review 2026-06-03, 6 attackers + synth). REFRAME (confirmed): uncompute correctness is a unitarity theorem (U†U=I) validated by construction + gate-sequence fixtures like every other gate — NOT a simulator gap. The whole risk is the GATE admitting an unsafe case. Spec defines an 8-layer CONSERVATIVE gate G0-G7 (decline on any failure): G0 npu.1 structure/identity; G1 base is a direct cq_theta (not select/phi/arg/data-op); G2 single-Ry (classical arg0, reject chained theta); G3 no extra mutation between prep and merge (reject theta-then-cq_phi Rz garbage); G4 no direct-to-merge default for a distinct-base mux phi; G5 variable-angle dominance; G6 cross-phi base disjointness + region-wide LIVENESS (no-cloning / dead-after-merge — this absorbs the liveness angle); G7 uniform width across mux bases. Plus prerequisites (the 7 cqrt_ry_*_controlled_inv + WidthDispatch resolver + DominatorTree), the ATOMIC-LANDING requirement (gate+mux+uncompute+symbols are one indivisible commit, else revert to the npu.1 decline), the narrow happy-path that lowers, impl order, the positive+decline+regression fixtures, and 4 open risks. title: Phase 4.1 — gated multi-arm switch/if cascade (general side-effecting arms)
description:
Phase 4.1 follow-on (PRD §8.5, IMPL §13 WP18). The ONE multi-way shape that does NOT fold into the switch→select-chain normalization (-aht.1): a cascade of arms with ARBITRARY SIDE-EFFECTING gate bodies (distinct gate sequences / controlled arithmetic per case, not just a value or a rotation angle). There is no value to select — each arm's ops must become _controlled on its eq-flag.

Mechanism = controlled-region substitution: the Phase 4.3 WP8 symmetric two-content-arm diamond generalized to an N-way FALSE-arm chain. Compute N mutually-exclusive eq-flags (default = AND of negated flags, Toffoli ladder); control each arm's gates on its flag via LIFO cqrt_x brackets; dissolve φ via WP7's multi-φ path. This is the CQ analog of Bennett.jl's _expand_switches br-cascade — the Option-B fallback.

SEPARATE from -aht.1's select-chain unit (different mechanism — do not conflate). RED: lowering_control_switch_gated.ll (switch(q) whose arms apply distinct gate sequences to an external handle). DONE: gated multi-arm switch lowers to per-arm controlled gates; no residual switch/br i1 on a handle. Depends on u6v.1 (multi-φ dissolution) + u6v.2 (symmetric diamond).
notes:
CLARIFICATION (2026-06-02): this is an IMPLEMENTATION task, NOT a Bennett.jl import and NOT a from-scratch research spike. Bennett is a REFERENCE only — no Julia dependency. The "Option-B fallback" (br-cascade) means a CQ-side C++ desugaring modeled on Bennett's _expand_switches IDEA, reimplemented in our own LLVM pass — never linking or subprocessing Bennett. The mechanism is already chosen: generalize the Phase 4.3 WP8 symmetric two-content-arm controlled substitution to an N-way false-arm chain.

BUT the design is lighter than -aht.1's, so START WITH A DIAGNOSE-FIRST SPIKE: empirically confirm the gated-cascade shape actually survives clang -O1. We have NOT pinned the exact -O1 output the way the Phase 4.3 audit did for the 44 if-shapes; arbitrary side-effecting per-case bodies are *believed* not to fold into selects/angle-selects, but verify before implementing. Only after the shape is pinned, implement the WP8 generalization.

No urgency / no risk while open: the shape is currently SAFE — loud-diagnosed by the WP12 / u6v.6 tainted-switch guard (no silent miscompile).
close_reason: Diagnose-first spike done on real clang -O1 IR: gated cascade survives as a SwitchInst (safe). WP18 implemented — gated multi-arm switch → N-way controlled substitution (per-case eq-flags, default on ¬OR, reuse substituteArm, N-way φ dissolution, linearize). Commit ff13ead. Fixture switch_gated now POSITIVE. Spike also fixed a silent miscompile (jump-table, commit 859fc50). Follow-ons filed: 5zu (jump-table lowering), 509 (default-direct/sparse). Adjacent P1 found in review filed separately (double-φ angle).

title: Mixed-arm select mux (one classical arm) via the existing HH controlled adder
description:
SHAPE: `select i1 %f, A, B` with the condition tainted and EXACTLY ONE value arm
tainted (a handle); the other arm classical (constant or runtime variable).
Real -O1 of example/test_control.c:
  %1    = icmp sgt i32 %h, -3
  %h_op = cq_template_sub_i32_lh(i32 9, i32 %h)        ; the tainted true arm (12 - a)
  %2    = select i1 %1, i32 %h_op, i32 -3              ; B = -3 is classical

CONSTRUCTION (mirrors the WP4 classical-arm reduction, PRD §2.6, with HL->HH and a
register delta). Let C be the classical arm, Q the tainted arm; ctrl = flag if Q is the
true (flag=1) arm, else the complemented flag (see below):
  1. delta = Q - C  as a REGISTER, via the existing UNCONTROLLED data template
     cq_template_sub_<W>_hl(Qhandle, Cclassical)  (no controlled form needed here).
  2. regC = cqrt_alloc_<W>(Cclassical)            (seed from the classical arm).
  3. Res  = cq_template_add_<W>_controlled(ctrl, regC, delta)   ; the HH controlled add.
     Resolver: ControlledSymbols::controlledDataTemplateFn("add", W, Shape::QQ,
     /*inverse=*/false) -> (flag, handle, handle); name = cq_template_add_<W>_controlled.
  4. RAUW the select to Res; register Res tainted + BirthOrder slot (dissolveSelect
     already does this for the classical/classical path).
Result = C + ctrl·(Q - C) = ctrl ? Q : C. For the example (Q=12-a, C=-3, ctrl=flag):
-3 + flag·((12-a)-(-3)) = flag ? (12-a) : -3. Correct.

CONTROL SENSE: if the CLASSICAL arm is the TRUE arm (select i1 %f, C, Q), seed regC and
control on the complemented flag (cqrt_x(f) bracket, uncomputed LIFO — reuse §2.5
ControlledSymbols::xFn), so result = C + ¬f·(Q-C) = f ? C : Q. (Or equivalently swap and
keep flag — pick one and pin it in the fixture.)

PASS TOUCH-POINTS (no runtime/gen_templates change):
  - ir-pass/src/ControlDetection.cpp detectControlRegions: the SelectRegion gate
    currently rejects ANY tainted arm:
       if (taint.Tainted.count(Sel->getTrueValue()) ||
           taint.Tainted.count(Sel->getFalseValue())) continue;   // line ~311
    Relax to accept EXACTLY ONE tainted arm (keep rejecting both-tainted -> that is
    child .2). Record on the ControlRegion which arm is the classical seed and the
    control sense.
  - ir-pass/src/MergeDissolution.cpp dissolveSelect: add a tainted-arm branch. Instead
    of the host Builder.CreateSub(A,B) + Shape::HL controlled add (the
    [classical,classical] path, kept as-is), build `delta` via the uncontrolled
    sub_<W>_hl template and call the Shape::QQ controlled add.
  - The feeding icmp lowers as the control flag exactly as in the WP3/WP4 path
    (ControlFlag); it does NOT go down the data-position CompareLowering path
    (isDataPositionCompare already bails on a select-condition compare).

UNCOMPUTE: delta and the arm register are data temporaries -> Phase 5 frees them
(unchanged). Phase 4 still brackets only the control flag (+ the ¬f X-bracket when the
classical arm is the true arm).

RED fixture: lowering_control_mux_mixed_i32.ll (a mixed-arm tainted select) currently
passes through un-lowered. GREEN: lowers to alloc + sub_hl + add_controlled, opt -verify
clean. Add an e2e slice (clang -O1 -> opt cq-lowering -> link -> run) diffing a golden
trace, modeled on e2e-slice-control-merge.

CAVEAT: template bodies are trace stubs for ALL templates (real bodies post-freeze) —
ABI-level existence, same status as the classical-arm reduction already shipped.
acceptance_criteria: A mixed-arm 'y=(q>0)?f(q):C' program lowers to cqrt_alloc + cq_template_sub_*_hl + cq_template_add_*_controlled (Shape::QQ); LIT fixture + e2e slice green; opt -verify clean; WP3-WP6 byte-identical.
close_reason: Mixed-arm select mux implemented (gate relaxed + dissolveSelect QQ branch); LIT + e2e green; WP3-WP6 byte-identical. Reviewer ACCEPT.

description:

`cq_template_<op>_<W>_controlled(flag, a_handle, b_handle)` and its `_controlled_inv`

title: WP5 — Compound (&& / ||) + nested control (single-flag AND model)
description: RED: lowering_control_and_i32.ll (select i1 %fa, i1 %fb, i1 false), lowering_control_or_i32.ll (select i1 %fa, i1 true, i1 %fb), lowering_control_nested_i32.ll (an if inside an if) -> untouched flag-selects / un-combined nested flags against WP4. GREEN: ControlDetection recognizes the i1-select-over-flags idiom as a FLAG COMBINATION (not a data select): AND = select i1 %fa, i1 %fb, i1 false; OR = select i1 %fa, i1 true, i1 %fb (PRD §2.5); for nesting the inner region carries ParentFlag=outer.Flag, Depth=outer.Depth+1. FlagConjunction combineFlags(fa,fb,kind): AND -> fresh ancilla f=cqrt_alloc_i1(0) then cqrt_toffoli(fa,fb,f); OR -> De Morgan cqrt_x(fa);cqrt_x(fb);cqrt_toffoli(fa,fb,f);cqrt_x(f);cqrt_x(fa);cqrt_x(fb); Nesting -> identical AND of ParentFlag with inner flag into f_both, inner ops control on f_both (depth-N reuses depth-1 verbatim, PRD §2.7). ControlledLowering pushes each conjoined flag on the LIFO stack and uncomputes in reverse (cqrt_toffoli_inv + the Xs), innermost first (risk R4); the nested fixture asserts compute/uncompute order.

title: WP3 — Single-armed gate (br-diamond): headline shape end-to-end
description: First behavioral WP and the integration spine (six new control TUs). A tainted if (q>k) y=gate(y); arriving as a br-diamond + phi[modified,original] lowers to a controlled rotation, the phi dissolves to the in-place handle, the diamond linearizes, flag bracketed. RED: ir-pass/test/lowering_control_gate_br_i32.ll (from real clang -O1) -> diamond untouched against WP2. GREEN: ControlDetection (ControlPlan detectControlRegions(M,taint): recognize 2-block diamond+merge phi, build ControlRegion, insert arm cq_phi into InShadow; LOUD DiagnosticInfoUnsupported on ret/measure/out-of-region br escape, PRD §5; pure analysis). RotationLowering edit: HandleWidth[H]=abiWidthFromType(Op->getType()) at the mint; skip in-shadow cq_phi; factor emitRz(handle,angle,controlled,flag). title: Phase 4.1 — quantum-controlled escape (return/break/goto + measurement in shadow)
description: A tainted-branch arm that escapes the region — if(q) return...; / break / goto, or a cq_measure inside the arm — gates an escape rather than an in-place gate, so it is not a clean controlled shadow. Verified 2026-06-01: 'if (q) return a;' compiles to br + phi where one arm returns and the other measures (phi [measure(x), a]). Structural cousin of the prototype uncompute pass's ReturnInst escape check (computeFreePoint returns null on a ret user). DECISION: reject with a source-located diagnostic ('measurement/return under quantum control') vs. opt-in -fcq-measurement-bridge (backend.md §7). Acceptance: escape cases emit the chosen diagnostic (or bridge) with correct source location; negative LIT fixtures. Depends on Phase 4 core.
notes:
Audit 2026-06-02: plain 'if(q) return' and measure-in-arm DIAGNOSE cleanly today (good). BUT goto/break out of a tainted arm CRASH instead — -O1 reshapes them into multi-phi diamonds that hit Phase 4.3 Family A (u6v.1) before the escape guard fires. So this refinement now also covers goto/break, and depends on Family A landing (then they either lower or reach the escape diagnostic).
VERDICT FINALIZED 2026-06-02 (PRD §8.6, IMPL §13 WP17): REJECT-by-default is CORRECT and confirmed by the Julia stack + literature — the terminal state, not a stopgap.

- Measurement under quantum control: reject PERMANENTLY. Bennett.jl has no measure op (classical→reversible; measurement lives in Sturm/Orkan); Sturm forbids measure/return inside when(q); Silq's rejected `condMeas` IS this exact program (a measure gated on a superposed predicate is unphysical — you'd have to measure the control first).
- return/break/goto under quantum control: reject by default. Bennett cfg.jl raises a loud error on non-reconverging exits ("lower_loop!: IRRet in loop body … not supported"). Quantum Control Machine (arXiv:2304.15000) proves a superposed jump/return is non-injective and cannot be a unitary; necessary+sufficient = injectivity + synchronization (all branches reconverge). Janus Structured Reversible Program Theorem: banning arbitrary goto/break/return loses NO expressive power — refactor.

-fcq-measurement-bridge: accept ONLY as an explicit opt-in DEMOTION to classical control via deferred measurement — insert the measure AT THE REGION BOUNDARY (collapse predicate before body), loud diagnostic, and STATICALLY REJECT re-entry of the measured value into a still-coherent region (= Silq's sanctioned fix / OpenQASM-3 feed-forward). Sold as a transparent "same if" lowering it is an ANTI-PATTERN (silently changes observable behavior; Silq/Q#/Quipper refuse it).

FUTURE (capture only, not this phase): return/break via DONE-FLAG predication for the BOUNDED + RECONVERGING subset — retval register + done ancilla; write retval & set done on the exit predicate; control every post-exit op on ¬done; final return writes retval on ¬done; UNCOMPUTE done at exit (recompute predicate from live args, CNOT off) or it leaks as garbage entangled with the result. QCM/Tower/if-conversion. True non-reconverging escape stays rejected.

Sturm ships the DUAL — deferred_measurement.jl (measure-then-classical-branch → controlled gate, true=control/false=anti-control, Nielsen-Chuang §4.4) — a collapse-free optimization worth a SEPARATE future pass. The break/goto crash path is already handled by the u6v.8 catch-all diagnostic.
close_reason: WP17 — escape verdict: reject-by-default for return/measure/break/goto under quantum control, now SOURCE-LOCATED via !dbg (PRD §8.6, confirmed by Julia stack + QCM/Silq/Janus). Commit bdb7f2f. Negative fixtures: escape_measure/break/goto/dbg (+ existing escape return). The -fcq-measurement-bridge opt-in is intentionally deferred (frontend-flag + cross-region analysis; verdict flags the transparent form as an anti-pattern).

title: Phase 4.1 — tainted `switch` lowering (N-way quantum branch)
description: clang -O1 preserves a real switch instruction + N-way phi for switch(q) on a tainted scrutinee (verified 2026-06-01: 'switch i32 %q [...]' + 3-way phi survived -O1). Phase 4's select/br normalization does not cover it. Options: (a) DEFAULT — pre-run stock LLVM -lowerswitch before cq-lowering, folding the switch into icmp-eq chains + selects/brs so it collapses into shapes Phase 4 already handles; (b) native multi-way controlled mux (control on q==0, q==1, ...). Acceptance: a switch(q) program lowers to the expected controlled trace; LIT fixture pins the chosen normalization. Depends on Phase 4 core.
notes:
Audit 2026-06-02 (PRD §7 Family E): the 'pre-run stock -lowerswitch' default is NOT free. -lowerswitch emits a balanced pivot TREE (icmp slt/eq + br with SHARED MULTI-PRED phi-merges); matchDiamond accepts a shared multi-pred merge -> linearization frees a still-referenced block -> CRASH. Surviving switch (no lowerswitch) silently miscompiles (branches on quantum handle id) — now guarded by Phase 4.3 Family D diagnostic (u6v.6). Switch lowering here depends on Phase 4.3 A (u6v.1) + C (u6v.2) landing first AND a NEW closed-diamond guard in matchDiamond (require merge has exactly 2 preds = Pred,Arm); then re-verify the pivot-tree path.
DIRECTION FINALIZED 2026-06-02 (PRD §8.2, IMPL §13 WP15): switch lowering = data-flow SELECT-CHAIN normalization, NOT -lowerswitch. A `normalizeTaintedSwitch` step (between taint-prop and region detection) rewrites a tainted-scrutinee SwitchInst + N-way merge φ into `icmp eq` flags + a nested `select` chain, then the EXISTING dissolveSelect/reduceClassicalMux path lowers it (icmp-eq HL flags + classical-mux/mux.1 controlled adds).

Supersedes Family E ("-lowerswitch + closed-diamond guard"): the select form never produces br-diamonds, so it sidesteps the pivot-tree shared-multi-pred-merge CRASH this issue's own notes found, AND needs no N-way φ dissolution (φ collapses to binary selects) and no new ABI.

Confirmed against Bennett.jl `_expand_switches` (fetched+verified 2026-06-02): same "eliminate switch by reduction" move, but Bennett targets a br-cascade because its downstream is gate-emission-over-CFG; CQ targets selects because downstream is opcode-replacement-over-dataflow. CQ also never inherits Bennett's U11 global-φ-incoming-rewrite trap (we read then DELETE the φ; merge becomes single-pred).

Scope: first cut = value-merge, break-terminated, clean reconverge (merge preds = case/default only). Also covers multi-way value `if` for FREE (PRD §8.3) and angle-switch via angle-select-chain (NEW WP16, generalizes u6v.4/WP10). Gated SIDE-EFFECTING multi-arm cascade is split to a NEW follow-on (different mechanism: controlled substitution / Bennett br-cascade fallback). Gate-level depth opt (unary iteration / QROM, arXiv:1805.03662) is BELOW the cqrt_* ABI = runtime concern, not this issue. Depends: u6v.1 (multi-φ infra) + u6v.4 (angle-select).
close_reason: WP15 (value-merge switch → select-chain via normalizeTaintedSwitch) + §8.3 (multi-way value if for free) + WP16 (angle-select-chain). Commits a69c247, 18027c4. Fixtures: switch_lower, multiway_if, angle_switch (+ angle_chain_nonexcl negative).

Cover: (a) taint as the implicit Q/C boundary (no keyword); (b) what triggers taint and how it propagates through LLVM ops; (c) mixed-operand semantics (Q+C ops route to dedicated runtime entry point + IR-pass dispatch, never promote classical to handle — see bd memory cq-mixed-operand-runtime-dispatch); (d) conversion semantics — casts are representation-only, never measure; (e) why this design solves function-lifting-with-hidden-casts (the diagnosis that motivated the redesign).
close_reason: Closed

title: Write docs/backend.md — new-design backend guideline
description: Backend = LLVM IR pass + runtime. Already validated in prototype/ + ir-pass/; document the existing mechanism under the new design's framing. Cover: (a) taint propagation from cq_* intrinsic sources through stock LLVM ops; (b) qint_mid_t struct-at-boundary signal mechanism; (c) lowering to handle-based cqrt_* runtime calls; (d) PostDominatorTree auto-uncomputation; (e) call-graph specialization; (f) cq_when_* region handling; (g) per-op compile-time adjoints. Pull surviving content from old docs/backend.md + old docs/architecture.md §6–§10.
close_reason: Wrote docs/backend.md (1131 lines, 14 sections). Documents IR pass + runtime under taint-driven design: input contract for Stage 4 IR (no qint_mid_t/cq_init_/cq_when_), forward taint propagation from cq_theta returns, gate-triggered allocation with operand-state dispatch, opcode lowering with _hl mixed-operand dispatch, call-graph specialization (curated symbol substitution + clone-on-taint), structural controlled-form lowering via PostDominatorTree, per-op uncomputation, mechanical adjoints (forward+controlled shipped only), manual inversion, 15-symbol runtime ABI, autogenerated template library, multi-file LTO flow. Cross-refs to frontend.md/quantum-classical-handling.md/example.md as forward refs (siblings still open: okm/7y8).

title: Write docs/frontend.md — new-design frontend guideline
description: Frontend under the taint-driven design is minimal: plain C + cq_* primitives from CQ.h, no rewriter. Cover: (a) intrinsic surface (cq_init, cq_alloc, cq_theta, cq_phi, cq_measure, cq_when_*, cq_invert_*); (b) what the user writes vs. what the IR pass derives from taint; (c) function lifting model — no hidden casts trigger measurement; (d) explicit cq_measure as the sole measurement sink; (e) cross-references to backend.md for lowering. Pull surviving content from old docs/architecture.md (now in archive).
close_reason: Wrote docs/frontend.md (523 lines, 9 sections). title: ir-pass: canonicalize Q+Q operand order by handle creation time
description: clang -O1 canonicalizes commutative add operands by SSA index, so the runtime trace for 'quantum int c = a + b;' depends on which handle was alloc'd first by clang's IR-numbering — currently worked_example traces (h1, h0) and full_example's Q+Q add traces (h4, h3). A future clang version could change this; the e2e harness uses byte-exact diff so we'd get spurious failures. Fix: in step 5 of CQLoweringPass.cpp, track handle creation order via a DenseMap<Value*, unsigned> BirthOrder (Allocs assigned in step 2, cq_template_add_i32 results assigned in step 5). When lowering a Q+Q add (both operands in Tainted), order the call's operands by BirthOrder so the older handle becomes lhs. This restores PLAN.md §4.7.1's canonical (h0, h1) format and makes the trace stable across clang versions. Refresh worked_example and full_example expected.log after landing.
close_reason: Closed

title: Phase 4 prototype: validate region handling (cq_when_*) on stock LLVM
description: Add a fourth pass cq-control that, within cq_when_begin/cq_when_end brackets, substitutes each cqrt_template_* call with its _controlled variant (taking the region's control handle as an additional first argument). Validates that region detection + controlled-variant substitution is implementable on stock LLVM, which is the one architectural mechanism (region handling) the existing Phase 2/5/7 prototypes have not touched.
design: cq-control operates on post-lowering IR (after cq-lowering has dissolved qint_mid_t and emitted cqrt_*). For prototype simplicity, the test input declares cq_when_begin as taking i32 directly (the handle), avoiding the qint_mid_t→handle resolution that real integration would need. Linear CFG only — begin and end in same BB. No nested regions. The mechanism: walk each BB, track 'current control' state, for each cqrt_template_* call inside a region emit a _controlled variant with the control prepended to args, erase brackets at end.
acceptance_criteria: 1. Pass plugin builds against stock LLVM 19 (additions only — existing passes unaffected). 2. opt-19 -load-pass-plugin -passes=cq-control runs without crash on hand-written post-lowering input. 3. Output passes opt -verify. 4. cq_when_begin and cq_when_end call sites erased. 5. cqrt_template_add_i32 inside the region is replaced by cqrt_template_add_i32_controlled with the control handle as the first argument. 6. cqrt_template_* calls OUTSIDE any region are NOT substituted (verified by adding a second template call after cq_when_end).
notes: Out of scope for this validation increment: qint_mid_t→handle resolution at cq_when_begin (would be an extension to cq-lowering); cross-BB regions (real cq_when_* can span branches); nested regions (multi-control accumulation); the inverse case cq_invert_begin/_end (separate but similar mechanism reusing emit_inverse from Phase 5). Companion: docs/architecture.md §5.1 + §7.5 (region brackets), docs/backend.md §5.9 (region handling spec).
close_reason: Phase 4 region-handling prototype succeeds. New cq-control pass (~80 LOC) walks each BB tracking cq_when_begin/end bracket state; for each cqrt_template_* call inside a region, substitutes the _controlled variant prepending the control handle. Test verifies: inside-region call replaced, outside-region call preserved, brackets erased, exactly 1 controlled call site + 1 plain call site. Linear single-BB regions only — nested + cross-BB regions deferred but use same stock LLVM API (BasicBlock iteration + IRBuilder + Module.getOrInsertFunction). See prototype/test/input_phase4.ll, run_test_phase4.sh.

title: Phase 5 multi-BB validation increment
description: Extend Phase 5 prototype with a test input that exercises non-trivial CFG (branched control flow, one handle used in both arms of an if). Verifies PostDominatorTree.findNearestCommonDominator correctly identifies the merge block as the post-dominator of all uses, and that cqrt_free is inserted at the merge point (not duplicated into either branch arm). Retires the only architectural-validation residual the original Phase 5 prototype did not exercise (it ran on linear single-BB IR).
design: Hand-crafted Stage 4 IR with one cq_init_i32 in entry block, branch to then/else arms that each measure the value, merge block with phi + ret. The handle's post-dominator is the merge block; algorithm should insert there. No code changes to cq_pass.cpp expected — this validates that the existing computeFreePoint() handles the multi-BB case correctly, which is the architecturally-novel question.
acceptance_criteria: 1. Pass plugin builds (no code changes needed — same cq-uncompute pass). 2. opt-19 -load-pass-plugin -passes='cq-lowering,cq-uncompute' on multi-BB input runs without crash. 3. Output passes opt -verify. 4. cqrt_free is emitted in the merge basic block (post-dominator of both arms). 5. cqrt_free is NOT emitted in either branch arm. 6. Output has exactly one cqrt_free per handle (no duplication).
notes: Companion: prototype/test/input.ll (linear case), prototype/test/run_test_phase5.sh (existing test). New: prototype/test/input_phase5_branch.ll + prototype/test/run_test_phase5_branch.sh. If the existing pass doesn't handle multi-BB correctly, that's a fix to make — but the design (findNearestCommonDominator + getFirstInsertionPt fallback) should already be correct.
close_reason: Phase 5 multi-BB validation succeeds. Hand-crafted Stage 4 IR with branch (entry → then/else → merge), one cq_init_i32 in entry, measure in both arms. opt-19 -passes='cq-lowering,cq-uncompute' produces exactly one cqrt_free emitted in the merge block (post-dominator) — not duplicated into either arm. PostDominatorTree.findNearestCommonDominator(then, else) correctly returns merge; getFirstInsertionPt() places the free at the right point (between phi and ret). No code changes were needed — existing computeFreePoint() handles multi-BB correctly. See prototype/test/input_phase5_branch.ll, run_test_phase5_branch.sh.

title: Phase 7 prototype: validate call-graph specialization on stock LLVM
description: Extend the prototype/ pass plugin with a third pass cq-specialize that demonstrates function cloning + call-site retargeting via stock LLVM CloneFunction / CloneFunctionInto + ValueToValueMapTy. For each call site with a qint_mid_t-typed argument, clone the callee, rename to __cq_q_<f>_q1, and retarget the call site. Validates that the Phase 7 mechanism (call-graph specialization synthesis) is implementable on stock LLVM with no fork.
design: Use CloneFunction(F, VMap) to clone the callee preserving signature. Set linkage to private/internal so DCE can remove the original if all uses are retargeted. Rename via Function::setName. Walk call sites of the original; for each whose arg is qint_mid_t-typed, replace setCalledFunction to the clone. Minimal scope: signature is preserved, no Bennett wrap-around (forward + CNOT-copy + reverse) — that is downstream implementation that uses the same already-validated emit_inverse mechanism from Phase 5. The point here is to confirm CloneFunction + call-site retargeting compose with the existing cq-lowering pass.
acceptance_criteria: 1. Pass plugin builds against stock LLVM 19 (no patches). 2. opt-19 -load-pass-plugin -passes=cq-specialize runs without crash on a test input with one function-call site. 3. Output IR passes opt -verify. 4. A new function named __cq_q_<original>_q1 exists in the module. 5. The clone has the same signature as the original (signature rewriting deferred). 6. The original call site is replaced with a call to the clone. 7. Both functions (original + clone) are well-formed.
notes: Out of scope: signature rewriting to (i32, i32) handle ABI, Bennett wrap-around (forward + CNOT-copy + reverse), specialization caching across multiple call sites, recursion handling, q-arg-mask discrimination beyond binary 'has qint_mid_t arg or not'. These are downstream once cloning + retargeting compose with lowering. Companion: bd memory prototype-validated-no-fork-2026-05-22, docs/llvm-fork-analysis.md §8.2.
close_reason: Phase 7 prototype validates call-graph specialization. cq-specialize pass uses stock LLVM CloneFunction (+ ValueToValueMapTy) to clone callees with qint_mid_t-typed args, renames via __cq_q_<f>_q1 mangling, retargets call sites. Test: opt-19 -load-pass-plugin -passes=cq-specialize produces a clone with internal linkage that preserves the original function's body shape (extractvalue + add + insertvalue + ret), call site in @example now references the clone, zero remaining calls to the original from @example, output passes opt -verify. See prototype/test/run_test_phase7.sh, prototype/test/output_phase7.ll.

title: Phase 5 prototype: validate auto-uncomputation on stock LLVM
description: Extend the prototype/ pass plugin with a second pass cq-uncompute that demonstrates last-use-driven uncomputation emission via stock LLVM PostDominatorTree analysis. For each handle SSA value (produced by cqrt_alloc_classical_i32 / cqrt_alloc_i32), compute the post-dominating last use and emit cqrt_free(handle) at that point. Skip handles that escape via ReturnInst. Validates that the Phase 5 mechanism (per-op compile-time adjoints at SSA live-range ends) is implementable on stock LLVM with no fork.
design: Use FunctionAnalysisManagerModuleProxy to obtain PostDominatorTreeAnalysis from a Module pass. Use PostDominatorTree::findNearestCommonDominator over user blocks to find the post-dominator BB; within that BB, find the latest user (linear case) and insert after. Emit cqrt_free as a placeholder for the full adjoint gate sequence — the real inverse template is downstream implementation work, not architecture validation. Single test input (same as main prototype) is sufficient: linear control flow exercises the API without needing complex CFG yet.
acceptance_criteria: 1. Pass plugin builds against stock LLVM 19 (no patches). 2. opt-19 -load-pass-plugin -passes='cq-lowering,cq-uncompute' runs without crash on input.ll. 3. Output IR passes opt -verify. 4. Each handle (cqrt_alloc_classical_i32 result, cqrt_alloc_i32 result) has a cqrt_free(handle) call emitted after its last use. 5. Handle SSA values that escape via ret are not freed. 6. Total pass plugin C++ remains focused (no bloat).
notes: Out of scope: real adjoint gate-sequence emission (cqrt_free as placeholder only), loop-aware uncomputation, multi-BB region uncomputation, multi-width. These are downstream once the core analysis-manager wiring is shown to work. Companion: bd memory prototype-validated-no-fork-2026-05-22, docs/llvm-fork-analysis.md §8.2.
close_reason: Phase 5 prototype validates auto-uncomputation. cq-uncompute pass uses stock LLVM PostDominatorTree (via FunctionAnalysisManagerModuleProxy) to compute the post-dominating last use of each handle, emits cqrt_free at that point, skips handles that escape via ret. Test pipeline: opt-19 -load-pass-plugin -passes='cq-lowering,cq-uncompute' produces 3 cqrt_free calls (one per handle), output passes opt -verify, all checks green. See prototype/test/run_test_phase5.sh, prototype/test/output_phase5.ll.

title: Candidate->control cascade: a Phase-6 spec candidate whose RESULT feeds an onward tainted-condition control region
description:
Physics-valid remaining safe over-decline in the dugh Phase-4x6 arc (the sibling of 9paa/afmv, which handle a spec candidate READING a merge/control rail). Here the candidate's RESULT is the quantum value that feeds further control.

SHAPE: a control-merge %out feeds a Phase-6 spec candidate g(%out) (round-1 Pending or round-2 new), and g's RESULT %z = call @g(%out) then feeds a DOWNSTREAM tainted-condition control region: if(%z>k){...} / switch(%z){...} / %z>k ? a : b.

CURRENT BEHAVIOR / ORDERING TENSION: in repropagateControlMerges, %out re-taints so %z (the call result) taints, then detectAndLowerOnwardControl (yn71) sees the tainted-condition region on %z. But g is NOT cloned/Bennett-wrapped until the step-262 driver (specialize), which runs AFTER repropagateControlMerges. So the downstream control region is adjudicated while %z is still  — a not-yet-reversible user-function-call result, not a lowered cqrt_* handle. The region either lowers routing on that raw %z (fragile) or loud-declines. The spec re-plan/re-detect (replanReseedSpecialization / detectSpecializations) only update plan6.Pending; they do not emit the clone, so the clone's ReturnTainted/handle identity is unknown at control-lowering time.

RULE-13 STATUS (verified SAFE 2026-07-05, the afmv-9paa combined workflow, switch-onward-ctl-phase-nest dimension SUB-CASE 3): every probe of this shape resolved to a correct bare-QQ/handle accept OR a safe loud decline (opt nonzero, 0-byte output, DiagnosticInfoUnsupported exits before any half-mutated IR is written) — NEVER a miscompile / crash / broken module. So this is a physics-valid over-decline (Prime Directive), NOT correctness debt.

PROPER HANDLING (design sketch, owner to scope): sequence so a spec candidate whose result feeds onward control is either (i) cloned/Bennett-wrapped BEFORE the downstream control region is lowered (a spec-then-control sub-ordering, or a combined fixpoint that clones eagerly), so the region routes on a genuine reversible handle with a known ReturnTainted; or (ii) explicitly + precisely declined at detection when a candidate's result feeds a tainted-condition region, with a dedicated message (rather than relying on the generic control decline over a raw call result). Needs its own PRD + red-green fixtures (accept: g(%out) result -> if(%z>k) phase arm; decline boundaries) + Rule-13 clearance (clone x control composition = a silent-miscompile class).

Relates to test_C_libtooling-9paa (candidate READS a rail), test_C_libtooling-afmv (round-1 Pending candidate reads a yn71 %out2 rail), yn71 (onward control), dugh (second propagation).

title: B: long double (f80/f128) width — unblock the 54 *l math.h variants (106→~160)
description:
The single biggest math.h coverage lever: 54 of the 65 cannot-yet math.h functions are the long double *l variants (sinl/cosl/powl/sqrtl/erfl/ceill/fmodl/fmal/ilogbl/atan2l/...), ALL blocked by one root cause. Verified 2026-07-01 vs tools/library_coverage/results.json: 54 blocked rows, uniform reason 'needs long double (f80/f128) source'. Landing this takes math.h 106 -> ~160/174. Width-only ABI extension (Rule 15: edit the YAML, regenerate); runtime is TRACE-ONLY so NO real f80 arithmetic is implemented -- only i32-handle/symbol plumbing. NOT a freeze gate (freeze gates are 7.1 wide-INTEGER widths, 7.5 QRAM ABI, 7.6 I/O tape); fp80/fp128 is additive coverage, freeze-orthogonal.

IMPORTANT nuance (verified 2026-07-01): the blocked *l rows fail TODAY at a _Generic COMPILE error ('controlling expression type long double not compatible with any generic association type'), because include/CQ.h has NO long double association at all -- NOT because backend f80 math is missing. So the blocker is layered: (1) frontend _Generic gap (always needed); (2) backend f80 width (needed only where long double==x86_fp80/fp128). Host check 2026-07-01: this machine is x86_64, long double==x86_fp80 (16B), so BOTH layers are needed here.
design:
Concrete work surface (verified 2026-07-01):
1. include/CQ.h -- _Generic STOPS at f64/f16 (no long double). Add long double -> cq_theta_f80 / cq_phi_f80 / cq_measure_f80 (per-target symbol; see platform policy).
2. ir-pass/src/OpcodeSupport.cpp -- abiWidthFromType: add ty->isX86_FP80Ty()->'f80' and ty->isFP128Ty()->'f128' (today only isHalfTy/isFloatTy/isDoubleTy). fpBits: f80=80, f128=128.
3. ir-pass/src/WidthDispatch.cpp -- suffix->width table (~:37), typeForWidth (Type::getX86_FP80Ty/getFP128Ty), and the dead-decl symbol sweep list (~:468: cq_theta_f80/cq_phi_f80/cq_measure_f80).
4. runtime: tools/opcode_table.yaml + tools/libm_table.yaml add f80/f128 width rows; regenerate via tools/gen_templates.py; SHA-256 drift check (gen_templates.py --check) gates it. Add cqrt_alloc_f80/ry_f80/rz_f80/measure_f80 to the hand-written core ABI (runtime/cq_runtime.{h,c}).
5. Angle fence ALREADY generalizes to >64-bit (WidthDispatch.cpp:139) -- f80/f128 as a rotation angle already declines; NO new angle hazard.

PLATFORM POLICY (decide up front): long double is x86_fp80 on x86-64 (this host; datalayout f80:128), fp128 on AArch64 Linux, and f64 (==double) on Apple Silicon / MSVC. The _Generic maps the C long double token to ONE runtime symbol, so the seed width must track the TARGET ABI. On long-double==double targets, ONLY step 1 is needed (maps to cq_theta_f64, zero backend change). v1 recommendation: support x86_fp80 (f80) for this host; carry f128 as a parallel width for AArch64.
acceptance_criteria: abiWidthFromType recognizes x86_fp80->f80 (and fp128->f128); tainted *l math.h variants lower instead of declining 'unsupported width'. CQ.h _Generic seeds long double. Positive lit fixture(s) for a long double slice (tainted long double add + a libm *l e.g. sqrtl) + >=1 e2e golden smoke. NEGATIVE preserved: a long double value as a rotation angle STILL declines (angle fence). gen_templates.py --check drift passes; runtime archives build. Coverage regenerated (probe.py run) -- the *l bucket flips blocked->verified. Rule-13 cleared (width-only but touches FROZEN ABI surfaces + the frontend seed).

title: Q/C boundary: tainted control compare with a 2nd non-branch (data) use yields a duplicate flag mint
description:
WI-5 §8 review NIT (Lens 3), confirmed verify-clean & memory-safe — NOT a 4.3 regression (pre-existing, affects the flat 4.1/4.2 path too via the identical use_empty guard in flattenRegion).

SHAPE: a tainted control compare used by BOTH a br AND a non-branch data consumer, e.g. C 'int f=(q>5); if(q>5){...}; return f+...;' → clang -O1 CSEs to one 'icmp sgt %q,5' with two uses (br + zext-to-i32). flattenRegion/flattenRegionTree's use_empty() guard correctly does NOT erase the compare (it has a live data use), and lowerOps then re-lowers the surviving tainted compare into a SECOND cq_template_icmp flag mint. Result: two icmp flag handles — one routed/stripped/freed (control), one leaked (the data compare). opt -verify clean, exactly the expected cqrt_free count, no UAF/double-free.

WHY IT MATTERS: a quantum-derived compare bit consumed as classical i32 data is a Q/C-boundary question that arguably should be adjudicated by declineTaintEscapes / data-position handling (isDataPositionCompare returns false when the compare feeds a br, so the data path skips it — but lowerOps still mints it), not silently lowered with a leaked handle. No demonstrable wrong unitary; precision/leak issue only.

REPRO: /tmp/adv_outer_cmp_extra.ll (constructed during the review) — 'br i1 %c1' + 'zext i1 %c1 to i32' → two cq_template_icmp_sgt_i32_hl calls.

SCOPE: out of Phase 4.3; a general control-path Q/C-boundary precision item. Decide: decline loudly (compare feeds both control and data) vs. accept-with-shared-flag vs. status-quo (leak).
close_reason: All children closed (ziov.1 shared-flag accept; ziov.2 deferred-strip won't-fix; ziov.3 nested cond-data-use decline; ziov.4 cast lowerability). The Q/C-boundary cond-data-use family (duplicate-mint, measure-before-route, dead-lineage, nested, unlowerable-cast) is fully adjudicated. Sibling jvun (out-of-scope fcmp silent-mint, discovered reviewing ziov.4) also fixed.

title: InvokeInst-borne cq_theta/cq_measure never seeded as taint source/sink (dyn_cast<CallInst> gap)
description: PRE-EXISTING (found during the test_C_libtooling-udw §adversarial review, 2026-06-11, under-decline lens; UNRELATED to udw). TaintPropagation.cpp collectAndSeed() and isMeasureSink() use dyn_cast<CallInst>, which returns null on an InvokeInst. So a cq_theta_<sfx> reached via 'invoke' is never added to ThetaCalls and never seeded into Tainted (its result is treated CLASSICAL); a cq_measure_<sfx> via 'invoke' is never recognized as a sink. Consequences: an invoke'd theta never lowers (survives as an undefined @cq_theta extern -> Stage-3 LINK error, loud-ish) and its result, used downstream, propagates no taint. Plain C + clang -O1 with NO exceptions emits 'call', not 'invoke', so this is not reachable from the supported frontend today (hence P3) — but the pass should be robust: either handle CallBase uniformly or loudly decline an invoke of a front-end intrinsic. NOTE the taint-escape guard already uses dyn_cast<CallBase> (catches invokes of UNKNOWN callees), so the gap is specifically the SOURCE/SINK seeding, not the escape side. Fix: switch collectAndSeed/isMeasureSink to CallBase, or add an explicit 'front-end intrinsic via invoke' decline. Add a decline (or accept) fixture.
close_reason: Closed
