title: MeasureLowering: wrong-prototype user declaration of @cq_measure_* drives a broken-module abort — add a signature check at collection time
description: Found during test_C_libtooling-5j5 review (2026-06-10), pre-existing and lift-independent. A user-declared @cq_measure_f64 with the wrong prototype (e.g. declared returning i32) drives MeasureLowering into emitting a mistyped replacement; the final opt verifier catches it (abort, no output) — LOUD, never silent, so no miscompile — but the failure surface is an LLVM 'Broken module' abort instead of the pass's source-located DiagnosticInfoUnsupported dialect. Reproduces on straight-line IR with no phi/control flow. Fix: validate the declared cq_measure_* (and plausibly cq_theta_*/cq_phi_* — audit all collection sites in MeasureLowering/TaintPropagation/WidthDispatch's 42-name surface) signature at collection time and decline loudly ('cq measure lowering: unsupported ...') on mismatch, with Rule 12 reject fixtures mirroring the message. Low urgency: failure is already loud; this is diagnostic-quality, not soundness.
notes:
AUDIT (2026-06-10): single collection site = TaintPropagation::resolveSources (name-only M.getFunction over the 42-name surface); both pipeline entry points (run/runOnFunction) reach it via propagate(), so one guard covers the twin-pipeline trap. Empirical exposure map at HEAD: measure wrong-return -> Broken module abort 134 (headline); theta wrong-arg0 -> abort 134; theta MISSING ANGLE -> getArgOperand(1) out of range on no-assert LLVM, callee operand leaks into cqrt_ry as the angle, abort 134; phi wrong-angle-type -> abort 134; phi wrong-return on classical operand -> abort 134 (delete-path RAUW); theta wrong-return -> loud-but-misleading 'no template for opcode trunc' exit 1. ArmClassify/SwapRouteEmit prefix-matchers only run downstream of collected taint and after propagate's DS_Error exit - not independently exposed. cq_invert_* / __cq_invert_* are prefix-recognized escapes with no typed replacement minted - no exposure.

FIX: declMatchesPrototype + diagnoseMalformedDecl in resolveSources; canonical prototype per suffix = T(T,double) theta/phi, T(T) measure, T=WidthDispatch::llvmTypeFor; exact FunctionType match (no varargs/extra params; param ATTRIBUTES not in FunctionType so clang-emitted CQ.h decls pass). Mismatch -> per-concern dialect ('cq rotation lowering: unsupported declared prototype for <name>' / 'cq measure lowering: ...'), DS_Error, first call site's !dbg (decl itself when uncalled), decl NOT inserted into FnSets (in-process hosts: calls become opaque externs owned by the taint-escape guard).

PASSTHROUGH-BOUNDARY DECISION (deliberate, pinned by lowering_reject_decl_prototype_unused.ll): a wrong-prototype RESERVED name declines even with zero call sites - gating on 'has calls' would make the diagnostic depend on DCE happenstance; over-declining is safe. Unrecognized suffixes (cq_measure_xyz999) stay out of collection/validation entirely (probed: passthrough). Correct-prototype decl-only stays passthrough (probed byte-untouched). 4 Rule-12 reject fixtures added (measure/theta/phi/unused), red-confirmed at HEAD; ir-pass-lit 136 green; 6 e2e slices green.
close_reason: Closed

title: Lift the classical-mux over-decline for the one-register merge phi: if (classical_c) q = cq_phi(q, theta); measure(q)
description: Follow-up from test_C_libtooling-wi5 (2026-06-10, commit 510e397). declineClassicalMuxes now loudly declines ANY live select/phi reading tainted data — including a live merge phi whose distinct tainted incoming SSA values are semantically the SAME register (the natural 'classical if around a quantum gate' shape: if (classical_c) q = cq_phi(q, theta); use(q)). That shape survives clang -O1 (instcombine does NOT fold it — incomings are distinct SSA values), was silently accepted and runtime-correct in main at HEAD~1 (post-RAUW the phi collapses to identical handle incomings), and was FreePoint-loud in non-main functions. Now it declines loudly everywhere — over-decline, doctrine-safe, but it is the most natural classically-controlled-gate program a user will write. Deliberate lift candidates: (a) in declineClassicalMuxes, ACCEPT a live phi/select when every tainted incoming resolves (through the cq_phi/cq_theta arg-0 wire, cf. WireWalk) to ONE base handle AND the untainted incomings are the same wire's pre-gate value — i.e. the mux is a no-op on the handle domain post-RAUW; RAUW it to the handle eagerly and let normal lowering proceed; (b) assign the shape a real owner (classically-controlled gates are just... classical control over WHICH gates execute — the trace differs per shot, which is fine classically; verify against an oracle probe that the per-branch trace semantics is what the user wrote, no quantum-coherence hazard since the condition is classical). Rule 12: ship accept fixture(s) + decline complements (mux that does NOT resolve to one register stays declined). Statevector/Rule 13 clearance required for the accept predicate. Until then the loud decline is correct-by-doctrine (over-declining is always safe).
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: sorenwilkening
comments.text: LIFT LANDED (worker, pending review). Mechanism = candidate (a), RAUW-eagerly, refined: liftOneRegisterMergePhi in TaintPropagation.cpp, called from declineClassicalMuxes' phi branch (both entry points inherit it). ACCEPT PREDICATE (phi-only, 2-incoming): (1) live, (2) every incoming tainted, (3) both incomings resolve through the in-place rotation wire — peel arg-0 of COLLECTED cq_theta/cq_phi call sites (exact CallInst membership, never name match) while the operand is tainted; classical-operand theta = mint point = base — to ONE common base, (4) lazy per-function DT, (5) defensive classical-condition check on IDom + both pred terminators (ControlDetect ownership hygiene for in-process hosts), (6) every chain gate's parent == its edge's incoming block, (7a) no chain gate reaches the OTHER edge's terminator (kills classical-loop iteration-2 stale-base; pinned by phi_loop fixture), (7b) the gate's own edge terminator cannot reach back to the gate (kills applied-twice/recorded-once; every cycle through the gate exits via that terminator). Then RAUW phi -> base, scrub Tainted (SwapRouteEmit::scrubTaint precedent), erase. RAUW-not-leave-standing because leaving the phi regresses non-main to the FreePoint FirstUnrecognized decline; post-RAUW the module IS the phi-less form the pipeline already accepts (verified byte-level both main and non-main). SELECT REFUTATION (confirmed): SSA forces select operands to dominate it => a gate-call incoming has ALREADY FIRED unconditionally; the untaken incoming names a pre-gate record the one register no longer holds — lifting would compile 'rotate iff c' to 'always rotate' (wrong unitary). clang -O1 cannot even emit that select from the ternary (opaque call not speculatable — verified: both if-form and ternary compile to the SAME branch+phi). Selects stay categorically declined; pinned by select_onereg fixture. ARM-ADD stays declined: cq_template_add RAUWs to the template CALL result = FRESH rail, so the phi incomings post-lowering are DIFFERENT handles (real mux); resolver only peels rotations, by construction. Rule-13 clearance: classical condition = one path per shot; lift adds/moves/removes NO gate (only an SSA name dies); rz/ry stay INSIDE their arm so per-shot trace == executed source path; conditions 3/6/7 prove every edge's claimed record == physical wire state at the merge on every path. Adversarial probes beyond fixtures: degenerate same-value phi (accepts, identity), nested sequential diamonds (both lift, compose via BB-order RAUW), downstream tainted add over lifted phi (template at merge, per-path sound, Rz diagonal), tainted-angle arm gate (lift accepts, declineTaintedAngle still fires loud later), ret-escape non-main (Escaped, no free), f64 HANDLE wire (lifts — it is data, not an angle; lift keys on wire resolution, not width). Deliberate conservatisms (future lifts, file new issues if wanted): N>2 incomings (classical switch merges) and cross-block chains whose straight edge carries the chain tail — both per-edge provable but unfixtured. Fixtures: 4 accepts (onereg main / nonmain / theta_chain / ifelse) + 5 decline complements (select_onereg, phi_tworeg, phi_derived_add, phi_crossblock_chain, phi_loop) + e2e golden slice_classical_if_gate (goldens BOTH polarities in one run via argc>0 / argc>100). Full ctest 10/10.

title: Swap-route design: mint the control flag at the COMPARE's program point (lift the 'condition predates a non-diagonal gate' conservative decline)
description: The 9hh §8 clearance found (and conservatively declined) the chained-Ry stale-condition shape: c = (q>5); q = cq_theta(q, t2); if (c) {...}. The emitter mints the flag at the BRANCH position, so an intervening tainted-operand cq_theta (non-diagonal Ry) makes the mint read the post-Ry basis — wrong-arm selection with a CLEAN flag (verify-clean; oracle fidelity 0.848 vs source — clearance_derived_base.py negative probe 3). Landed guard: ArmClassify::nonDiagonalGateBeforeBranch declines 'condition predates a non-diagonal gate' on ANY tainted-operand theta between compare and branch, and on a compare outside the pred block (unbounded gap). This issue is the principled fix: mint the flag AT THE COMPARE's position (the source semantics point). NOTE the oracle also shows the source semantics itself has no sound flag-strip for that shape (mint-at-compare leaves the flag unstrippable after the Ry: P(flag=1)=0.118) — so mint-at-compare alone is NOT sufficient; the flag may need Bennett-style uncompute via reverse-play, or the shape may be fundamentally a decline. Treat as a design investigation, not a quick lift. Intervening DIAGONAL gates (cq_phi) remain fine (basis-preserving — the accepted stalecond fixtures).
close_reason: Closed

title: Both-arms-handle select mux (alloc-zero + two controlled adds; preserve reused arms)
description:
SHAPE: `select i1 %f, %hp, %hq` — condition tainted and BOTH value arms tainted handles.
The mixed-arm reduction (.1) cannot apply: cqrt_alloc seeds from a CLASSICAL value, and
here neither arm is classical.

CONSTRUCTION (still NO cswap/Fredkin needed — that is only an in-place alternative):
  1. regOut = cqrt_alloc_<W>(0).
  2. cq_template_add_<W>_controlled(f,  regOut, hp)     ; regOut += f·hp
  3. cqrt_x(f)                                          ; form ¬f (LIFO-bracketed)
     cq_template_add_<W>_controlled(f, regOut, hq)      ; regOut += ¬f·hq
     cqrt_x(f)                                          ; restore f
  Result = f·hp + ¬f·hq = f ? hp : hq.
Both hp and hq are READ (a_handle/b_handle operands), never consumed -> PRESERVED for
their other uses. This is the load-bearing difference from .1: an arm here may be live
elsewhere in the function, so a consuming/in-place strategy is unsafe; the additive
copy into a fresh ancilla preserves them.

PASS TOUCH-POINTS: extend the .1 detection gate to ALSO accept both-tainted; add the

title: Build -O-level regression matrix for stage-1 clang flag
description: Build a regression test matrix that lets the stage-1 clang -O level be raised above the validated -O1 floor with confidence. Per docs/frontend.md §8 'Optimization-level guidance', stage 1 is currently pinned at -O1 because higher levels introduce risks (aggressive inline pre-empting clone-on-taint; IPSCCP/argpromotion rewriting signatures; LoopUnroll/LoopVectorize on tainted loops; SimplifyCFG flattening branches the post-dom walk depends on; GVN CSE across tainted values; SLPVectorize fusing tainted+untainted scalars into a vector op at -O3). Matrix: small CQ programs compiled at -O0/-O1/-O2/-O3 (each), lowered IR diffed across levels, runtime gate sequences captured and compared. Goal: identify which risks fire in practice, which are theoretical, and whether the stage-1 default can move from -O1 to -O2/-O3 unconditionally or with specific -fno-* flags. Related: 5kb.
notes:
Re-deferred 2026-05-29 (pending Phase 3). Original deferral blockers ARE cleared: CQ.h has cq_theta/phi/measure; ir-pass targets @cq_theta_*; tests/e2e is a working end-to-end compile route. Probed the floor anyway — ran the full pipeline (clang -O$N -emit-llvm | opt cq-lowering | clang link | run) at -O0..-O3 on 6 probes (straightline/inline/loop/dup/slp/branch).

FINDINGS: -O0 correctly REJECTED by the pass (no mem2reg => taint stuck in allocas; floor confirmed from below). -O1==-O2==-O3 BYTE-IDENTICAL gate traces for all 6 probes — none of the frontend.md §8 risks fires. BUT the Phase-2 surface is too narrow to be a real test: only add/fadd lower, and 'if(flag){x=x+1}' collapses to an unconditional 'add; select i1' at -O1 *before the pass runs* (verified in IR), so there is no O1->O2 delta to catch. Real risks needing a verdict (SLPVectorize — clang declined to vectorize 2 i32 adds feeding opaque calls; LoopVectorize; IPSCCP/argpromotion signature rewrite; non-flattening guarded blocks) require the Phase-3 opcode surface (icmp/sub/mul/casts) + richer control flow. A green matrix today would over-claim.

RESUME when Phase 3 opcode lowering lands: build tests/omatrix/ then. Verified findings + corrected baseline in bd memory 'omatrix-baseline-macos'. (A prior in-session 'SimplifyCFG hazard fires' claim was WRONG — based on unread report files — now corrected; it does not fire on this surface.)

title: Investigate -O2/-O3 viability at stage 1 (post-rest)
description: Currently the pipeline pins clang -O1 at stage 1 (pre-IR-pass). -O1 is the validated floor — minimum needed for mem2reg/SROA cleanup. Higher levels are not prohibited by the design but introduce risks that need a test matrix. Defer until the rest of the taint-driven pipeline transition (frontend.md/backend.md/quantum-classical-handling.md/example.md/ROADMAP) is done.
notes: Stage 1 risks at -O2+: aggressive inline pre-empts clone-on-taint; IPSCCP/argpromotion can rewrite signatures; LoopUnroll/LoopVectorize on tainted loops/conditions; SimplifyCFG flattens branches the post-dom analysis walks; GVN CSE across tainted values. Stage 1 risks at -O3: SLPVectorize can fuse tainted + untainted scalar ops into a single vector op — would silently miscompile without vector-tainted-op template support. Stage 3 (post-pass codegen): any -O level safe — only stock LLVM ops + opaque cqrt_* externals remain; this is where most binary runtime perf comes from anyway. Recommendation: default -O1 stage 1, allow -O3 stage 3, require -fno-vectorize -fno-slp-vectorize if user pushes -O3 to stage 1 until vector-tainted templates exist. Need: regression test matrix (small CQ programs compiled at each -O level, lowered IR diffed, runtime gate sequences compared).

title: diagnoseMalformedDecl uses dyn_cast<CallInst> — invoke-only malformed reserved-name decl loses !dbg source location
description: PRE-EXISTING, ORTHOGONAL follow-up surfaced during the test_C_libtooling-rzs9 §adversarial review (completeness lens, 2026-06-11). TaintPropagation.cpp diagnoseMalformedDecl() walks F->users() with dyn_cast<CallInst> to pick the first call site for the DiagnosticInfoUnsupported function-context + !dbg. A malformed-prototype reserved-name decl (cq_theta_/cq_phi_/cq_measure_ with the wrong FunctionType) reached ONLY via 'invoke' (no plain-call users) finds no CallInst user and falls to the decl-level diagnostic (the F-context overload, no instruction !dbg) — STILL LOUD (opt exits non-zero), just without source-line precision. NOT a soundness issue: the precondition is a WRONG PROTOTYPE (orthogonal to rzs9's wrong CALL-FORM), a malformed decl never enters the FnSets, and clang -O1 on exception-free C never emits 'invoke' for opaque externs (doubly unreachable). Fix: switch the user scan to dyn_cast<CallBase> so an invoke'd call site supplies the !dbg, same generalization rzs9 applied to collectAndSeed/isMeasureSink. Diagnostic-precision hardening only — low priority. Add a fixture if fixed.
close_reason: Fixed: diagnoseMalformedDecl F->users() scan generalized dyn_cast<CallInst>->dyn_cast<CallBase> so an invoke-only malformed reserved-name decl supplies the caller function-context + invoke !dbg source location (was falling to the location-less decl-level <unknown>:0:0 overload). Same generalization rzs9 applied to collectAndSeed/isMeasureSink. Regression fixture lowering_reject_decl_prototype_invoke.ll (red-greens via mal.c:7:9 CHECK). Cleared by Rule-13 adversarial review (3-lens workflow); review caught a subagent-revert that had silently turned the edit into a no-op. Full ctest 11/11 green on a clean rebuild. Angle-skip CallInst sibling site analyzed + recorded as intentional (bd memory angle-skip-callinst-intentional) — NOT a soundness bug, left as-is.
